1.6.m: As he meditated, being self-conscious, a creation in five modes emerged; / it was completely enveloped in darkness, like a lamp covered by a jar, / devoid of external and internal light, motionless, and entirely insensate.

1.6.s:
yasmāttaiḥ saṃvṛtā buddhirmukhyāni karaṇāni ca.
tasmātte saṃvṛtātmāno nagā mukhyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..37..
1.6.d:
यस्मात्तैः संवृता बुद्धिर्मुख्यानि करणानि च।
तस्मात्ते संवृतात्मानो नगा मुख्याः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥37॥
1.6.m: Because their intellect and principal faculties were obstructed, / they, with their natures obscured, are known as stationary objects (*naga*s) or the primary creation (*mukhya*).

1.6.s:
mukhyasarge tathābhūtaṃ brahmā dṛṣṭvā hyasādhakam.
aprasannamanāḥ so'tha tato nyāso'bhyamanyata ..38..
1.6.d:
मुख्यसर्गे तथाभूतं ब्रह्मा दृष्ट्वा ह्यसाधकम्।
अप्रसन्नमनाः सोऽथ ततो न्यासोऽभ्यमन्यत ॥38॥
1.6.m: Seeing that the primary creation was thus inefficient for his purpose, / Brahmā became displeased in mind and thought of another creation.

1.6.s:
tasyābhidhyāyatastatra tiryyak sroto'bhyavarttata.
yasmāttiryag vyavartteta tiryyaksrotastataḥ smṛtam ..39..
1.6.d:
तस्याभिध्यायतस्तत्र तिर्य्यक् स्रोतोऽभ्यवर्त्तत।
यस्मात्तिर्यग् व्यवर्त्तेत तिर्य्यक्स्रोतस्ततः स्मृतम् ॥39॥
1.6.m: As he meditated on it, the transverse current (*tiryaksrotas*) came forth. / Because it moved horizontally (or crookedly), it is called *tiryaksrotas* [the animal world].

1.6.s:
tamobahutvātte sarvve hyajñānabahulāḥ smṛtāḥ.
utpathagrāhiṇaścāpi te dhyānāddhyānamāninaḥ ..40..
1.6.d:
तमोबहुत्वात्ते सर्व्वे ह्यज्ञानबहुलाः स्मृताः।
उत्पथग्राहिणश्चापि ते ध्यानाद्ध्यानमानिनः ॥40॥
1.6.m: Because darkness abounds in them, they are all known to have an abundance of ignorance; / they follow improper paths, and, although devoid of knowledge, they consider themselves knowledgeable.

1.6.s:
tiryyaksrotastu dṛṣṭvā vai dvitīyaṃ viśvamīśvaraḥ.
ahaṃkṛtā ahaṃmanā aṣṭāviṃśadvidhātmakāḥ ..41..
1.6.d:
तिर्य्यक्स्रोतस्तु दृष्ट्वा वै द्वितीयं विश्वमीश्वरः।
अहंकृता अहंमना अष्टाविंशद्विधात्मकाः ॥41॥
1.6.m: Seeing that the second creation of the universe, the *tiryaksrotas*, / was ego-driven, self-centered, and of twenty-eight varieties—

1.6.s:
ekādaśendriyavidhā navadhā codayastathā.
aṣṭau ca tārakādyāśca teṣāṃ śaktividhāḥ smṛtāḥ ..42..
1.6.d:
एकादशेन्द्रियविधा नवधा चोदयस्तथा।
अष्टौ च तारकाद्याश्च तेषां शक्तिविधाः स्मृताः ॥42॥
1.6.m: namely, eleven types of faculties, nine varieties of defects, / and eight types of powers such as *tāraka* and the like, which are regarded as their capacities—

1.6.s:
ataḥ prakāśāste sarvve āvṛtāśca bahiḥ punaḥ.
yasmāttiryak pravartteta tiryyaksrotāḥ sa ucyate ..43..
1.6.d:
अतः प्रकाशास्ते सर्व्वे आवृताश्च बहिः पुनः।
यस्मात्तिर्यक् प्रवर्त्तेत तिर्य्यक्स्रोताः स उच्यते ॥43॥
1.6.m: although they possess inner illumination, they are again veiled externally; / and since it proceeds crookedly, it is called *tiryaksrotas*.

1.6.s:
tiryaksrotāśca dṛṣṭvā vai dvitīyaṃ viśvamīśvaraḥ.
abhiprāyamathoddhūtaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvvantathābhidham.
tasyābhidhyāyato nityaṃ sāttvikaḥ samavarttata ..44..
1.6.d:
तिर्यक्स्रोताश्च दृष्ट्वा वै द्वितीयं विश्वमीश्वरः।
अभिप्रायमथोद्धूतं दृष्ट्वा सर्व्वन्तथाभिधम्।
तस्याभिध्यायतो नित्यं सात्त्विकः समवर्त्तत ॥44॥
1.6.m: Seeing the *tiryaksrotas*, the second creation of the universe, / and seeing that his intention had again failed in every respect, / as he constantly meditated, an entity characterized by goodness (*sattva*) came into being.

1.6.s:
ūrddhvasrotāstṛtīyastu sa caivorddhvavyavasthitaḥ.
yasmādvyavarttatohddhvantu ūrddhvasrotāstataḥ smṛtaḥ ..45..
1.6.d:
ऊर्द्ध्वस्रोतास्तृतीयस्तु स चैवोर्द्ध्वव्यवस्थितः।
यस्माद्व्यवर्त्ततोह्द्ध्वन्तु ऊर्द्ध्वस्रोतास्ततः स्मृतः ॥45॥
1.6.m: The third creation was the upward current (*ūrdhvasrotas*), and it stayed above; / because its current moved upward, it is known as *ūrdhvasrotas* [the divine world].

1.6.s:
te sukhaprītibahulā bahirantaśca saṃvṛtā.
prakāśā bahirantaśca ūrddhvasrotodbhavāḥ smṛtāḥ ..46..
1.6.d:
ते सुखप्रीतिबहुला बहिरन्तश्च संवृता।
प्रकाशा बहिरन्तश्च ऊर्द्ध्वस्रोतोद्भवाः स्मृताः ॥46॥
1.6.m: They abound in joy and pleasure, are not veiled internally or externally, / and are illuminated both inside and out; such are those born of the upward current.

1.6.s:
tena vā tādayo jñeyāḥ sṛṣṭātmāno vyavasthitāḥ.
ūrddhvasrotāstṛtīyo vai tena sargastu sa smṛtaḥ ..47..
1.6.d:
तेन वा तादयो ज्ञेयाः सृष्टात्मानो व्यवस्थिताः।
ऊर्द्ध्वस्रोतास्तृतीयो वै तेन सर्गस्तु स स्मृतः ॥47॥
1.6.m: By that, those established beings, created by him, are to be understood; / and because of that, that creation is remembered as the third, the upward current.

1.6.s:
ūrddhvasrotaḥsu sṛṣṭeṣu deveṣu sa tadā prabhuḥ.
prītimānabhavadbrahmā tato'nyaṃ so'bhyamanyata.
sasarjja sargamanyaṃ sa sādhakaṃ prabhurīśvaraḥ ..48..
1.6.d:
ऊर्द्ध्वस्रोतःसु सृष्टेषु देवेषु स तदा प्रभुः।
प्रीतिमानभवद्ब्रह्मा ततोऽन्यं सोऽभ्यमन्यत।
ससर्ज्ज सर्गमन्यं स साधकं प्रभुरीश्वरः ॥48॥
1.6.m: When the gods of the upward current were created, the Lord Brahmā / was pleased; then he contemplated another creation. / The Lord and master created another creation, which would be an effective agent.

1.6.s:
athābhidhyāyatastasya satyābhidhyāyinastadā.
prādurbbabhūva cāvyaktādarvvāk‌srotaḥ susādhakam.
yasmādarvākvyavartteta tato'rvvāksrota ucyate ..49..
1.6.d:
अथाभिध्यायतस्तस्य सत्याभिध्यायिनस्तदा।
प्रादुर्ब्बभूव चाव्यक्तादर्व्वाक्‌स्रोतः सुसाधकम्।
यस्मादर्वाक्व्यवर्त्तेत ततोऽर्व्वाक्स्रोत उच्यते ॥49॥
1.6.m: Then, as he who meditated upon truth continued to contemplate, / the downward current (*arvāksrotas*), which was well-suited for action, manifested from the unmanifest (*avyakta*). / Because it moves downward, it is called *arvāksrotas* [the human world].

1.6.s:
te ca prakāśabahulāstamaḥ sattvarajodhikāḥ.
tasmātte duḥkhabahulā bhūyo bhūyaśca kāriṇaḥ ..50..
1.6.d:
ते च प्रकाशबहुलास्तमः सत्त्वरजोधिकाः।
तस्मात्ते दुःखबहुला भूयो भूयश्च कारिणः ॥50॥
1.6.m: They have an abundance of light, but darkness (*tamas*), purity (*sattva*), and passion (*rajas*) predominate [variously] among them; / therefore they have an abundance of suffering, yet they perform actions again and again.

1.6.s:
prakāśā bahirantaśca manuṣyāḥ sādhakāśca te.
lakṣaṇaistārakādyaiste aṣṭadhā ca vyavasthitāḥ ..51..
1.6.d:
प्रकाशा बहिरन्तश्च मनुष्याः साधकाश्च ते।
लक्षणैस्तारकाद्यैस्ते अष्टधा च व्यवस्थिताः ॥51॥
1.6.m: These human beings have light both internally and externally, and they are effective agents; / by their characteristics beginning with *tāraka*, they are established in eight ways.

1.6.s:
siddhātmāno manuṣyāste gandharvasahadharmmiṇaḥ.
ityeṣa tejasaḥ sargo hyarvvāksrotāḥ prakīrttitaḥ ..52..
1.6.d:
सिद्धात्मानो मनुष्यास्ते गन्धर्वसहधर्म्मिणः।
इत्येष तेजसः सर्गो ह्यर्व्वाक्स्रोताः प्रकीर्त्तितः ॥52॥
1.6.m: Those human beings are accomplished souls (*siddha*s), sharing duties with the *gandharva*s. / Thus has been proclaimed the creation of fiery energy (*tejas*), which is the downward current.

1.6.s:
pañcamo'nugrahaḥ sargaścaturddhā sa vyavasthitaḥ.
viparyyayeṇa śaktyā ca tuṣṭyā siddhyā tathaiva ca.
vivṛttaṃ varttamānañca te'rthaṃ jānanti tattvataḥ ..53..
1.6.d:
पञ्चमोऽनुग्रहः सर्गश्चतुर्द्धा स व्यवस्थितः।
विपर्य्ययेण शक्त्या च तुष्ट्या सिद्ध्या तथैव च।
विवृत्तं वर्त्तमानञ्च तेऽर्थं जानन्ति तत्त्वतः ॥53॥
1.6.m: The fifth creation is the creation of favor (*anugraha*), which is arranged in four ways: / by error, disability, complacency, and perfection; / they know the past and the present reality in its true essence.

1.6.s:
bhūtādikānāṃ sattvānāṃ ṣaṣṭhaḥ sargaḥ sa ucyate.
viparyyayeṇa bhūtādiraśaktyā ca vyavasthitaḥ ..54..
1.6.d:
भूतादिकानां सत्त्वानां षष्ठः सर्गः स उच्यते।
विपर्य्ययेण भूतादिरशक्त्या च व्यवस्थितः ॥54॥
1.6.m: The creation of beings beginning with spirits (*bhūta*s) is called the sixth; / the class of *bhūta*s is characterized by error and disability.

1.6.s:
prathamo mahataḥ sargo vijñeyo mahatastu saḥ.
tanmātrāṇāṃ dvitīyastu bhūtasargaḥ sa ucyate ..55..
1.6.d:
प्रथमो महतः सर्गो विज्ञेयो महतस्तु सः।
तन्मात्राणां द्वितीयस्तु भूतसर्गः स उच्यते ॥55॥
1.6.m: The first creation should be known as that of the Great Principle (*mahat*); / the second is that of the subtle elements (*tanmātra*s), which is called the creation of the elements (*bhūtasarga*).

1.6.s:
vaikārikastṛtīyastu sarga aindriya kaḥ smṛtaḥ.
ityeṣa prākṛtaḥ sargaḥ sambhūto bhuddhipūrvakaḥ ..56..
1.6.d:
वैकारिकस्तृतीयस्तु सर्ग ऐन्द्रिय कः स्मृतः।
इत्येष प्राकृतः सर्गः सम्भूतो भुद्धिपूर्वकः ॥56॥
1.6.m: The third creation, born of transformation (*vaikārika*), is considered that of the sense organs (*aindriyaka*). / Thus is the elemental creation (*prākṛta sarga*) that arose preceded by intellect.

1.6.s:
mukhyasargaścaturthastu mukhyā vai sthāvarāḥ smṛtāḥ.
tiryyaksotāśca yaḥ sargastiryyagyoniḥ sa pañcamaḥ ..57..
1.6.d:
मुख्यसर्गश्चतुर्थस्तु मुख्या वै स्थावराः स्मृताः।
तिर्य्यक्सोताश्च यः सर्गस्तिर्य्यग्योनिः स पञ्चमः ॥57॥
1.6.m: The primary creation (*mukhyasarga*) is the fourth, and the primary are indeed the stationary things. / That which is the creation of the transverse current (*tiryaksrotas*) is the animal realm, the fifth.

1.6.s:
tathorddhvasrotasāṃ ṣaṣṭho devasargastu sa smṛtaḥ.
tathārvāksrotasāṃ sargaḥ saptamaḥ sa tu mānuṣaḥ ..58..
1.6.d:
तथोर्द्ध्वस्रोतसां षष्ठो देवसर्गस्तु स स्मृतः।
तथार्वाक्स्रोतसां सर्गः सप्तमः स तु मानुषः ॥58॥
1.6.m: And the sixth is that of the upward current (*ūrdhvasrotas*), which is known as the creation of the gods. / And the creation of the downward current (*arvāksrotas*), the seventh, is the human creation.

1.6.s:
aṣṭamo'nugrahaḥ sargaḥ sāttvikastāmasastu saḥ.
pañcaite vaikṛtāḥ sargāḥ prākṛtāstu trayaḥ smṛtāḥ ..59..
1.6.d:
अष्टमोऽनुग्रहः सर्गः सात्त्विकस्तामसस्तु सः।
पञ्चैते वैकृताः सर्गाः प्राकृतास्तु त्रयः स्मृताः ॥59॥
1.6.m: The eighth is the creation of favor (*anugraha*), which is both pure (*sāttvika*) and dark (*tāmasika*). / These five are secondary creations (*vaikṛta*), whereas three are known as primary (*prākṛta*).

1.6.s:
prākṛto vaikṛtaścaiva kaumāro navamaḥ smṛtaḥ.
prākṛtāstu trayaḥ sargāḥ kṛtāste buddhipūrvvakāḥ ..60..
1.6.d:
प्राकृतो वैकृतश्चैव कौमारो नवमः स्मृतः।
प्राकृतास्तु त्रयः सर्गाः कृतास्ते बुद्धिपूर्व्वकाः ॥60॥
1.6.m: The ninth creation, the Kaumāra, is considered both primary and secondary. / The three primary creations were produced preceded by intellect.

1.6.s:
buddhipūrvvaṃ pravarttante ṣaṭsargā brahmaṇastu te.
vistarānugrahaṃ sargaṃ kīrttyamānaṃ nibodhata ..61..
1.6.d:
बुद्धिपूर्व्वं प्रवर्त्तन्ते षट्सर्गा ब्रह्मणस्तु ते।
विस्तरानुग्रहं सर्गं कीर्त्त्यमानं निबोधत ॥61॥
1.6.m: Those six creations of Brahmā proceed preceded by intellect. / Hear now in detail of the creation of favor (*anugraha*) as it is recounted:

1.6.s:
caturddhāvāsthitaḥ so'tha sarvabhūteṣu kṛtsnaśaḥ.
viparyayeṇa śaktyā ca tuṣṭyā siddhyā tathaiva ca ..62..
1.6.d:
चतुर्द्धावास्थितः सोऽथ सर्वभूतेषु कृत्स्नशः।
विपर्ययेण शक्त्या च तुष्ट्या सिद्ध्या तथैव च ॥62॥
1.6.m: It is established in four forms among all living beings in their entirety: / by error, disability, complacency, and perfection.

1.6.s:
sthāvareṣu viparyāsastiryagyoniṣu śaktitā.
siddhātmāno manuṣyāstu tuṣṭirddeveṣu kṛtsnaśaḥ ..63..
1.6.d:
स्थावरेषु विपर्यासस्तिर्यग्योनिषु शक्तिता।
सिद्धात्मानो मनुष्यास्तु तुष्टिर्द्देवेषु कृत्स्नशः ॥63॥
1.6.m: In stationary beings there is error; in the animal species, disability; / human beings are endowed with perfection; and in the gods, there is complacency in full measure.

1.6.s:
ityete prākṛtāścaiva vaikṛtāśca nava smṛtāḥ.
sargāḥ parasparasyātha prakārā bahavaḥ smṛtāḥ ..64..
1.6.d:
इत्येते प्राकृताश्चैव वैकृताश्च नव स्मृताः।
सर्गाः परस्परस्याथ प्रकारा बहवः स्मृताः ॥64॥
1.6.m: Thus these nine creations, both primary and secondary, are recorded. / Furthermore, there are many varieties among them.

1.6.s:
agre sasarjja vai brahmā mānasānātmanaḥ samān.
sanandanañca sanakaṃ vidvāṃsaṃ ca sanātanam ..65..
1.6.d:
अग्रे ससर्ज्ज वै ब्रह्मा मानसानात्मनः समान्।
सनन्दनञ्च सनकं विद्वांसं च सनातनम् ॥65॥
1.6.m: In the beginning, Brahmā created mind-born sons equal to himself: / Sanandana, Sanaka, and the wise Sanātana.

1.6.s:
vijñānena nivṛttāste vaivartena mahaujasaḥ.
saṃbuddhāścaiva nānātvādapaviddhāstrayo'pite.
asṛṣṭvaiva prajāsargaṃ pratisargaṃ gatāḥ punaḥ ..66..
1.6.d:
विज्ञानेन निवृत्तास्ते वैवर्तेन महौजसः।
संबुद्धाश्चैव नानात्वादपविद्धास्त्रयोऽपिते।
असृष्ट्वैव प्रजासर्गं प्रतिसर्गं गताः पुनः ॥66॥
1.6.m: Possessed of great splendor, they turned away [from worldly creation] through spiritual knowledge, free from transformation; / having awakened and abandoned all three worlds because of their manifold nature, / without creating offspring, they entered into dissolution (*pratisarga*).

1.6.s:
tadā teṣu vyatīteṣu tadānyān sādhakāṃśca tān.
mānasānasṛjadbrahmā punaḥ sthānābhimāninaḥ.
ābhūtasaṃplavāvasthānnāmatastānnibodhata ..67..
1.6.d:
तदा तेषु व्यतीतेषु तदान्यान् साधकांश्च तान्।
मानसानसृजद्ब्रह्मा पुनः स्थानाभिमानिनः।
आभूतसंप्लवावस्थान्नामतस्तान्निबोधत ॥67॥
1.6.m: When they had departed, Brahmā then created other mind-born sons / to be effective agents, deities presiding over stations, / who remain until the dissolution of all elements. Hear them by name:

1.6.s:
āpo'gniḥ pṛthivī vāyurantarikṣaṃ diśastathā.
svargaṃ divaḥ samudrāṃśca nadān śailān vanaspatīn ..68..
1.6.d:
आपोऽग्निः पृथिवी वायुरन्तरिक्षं दिशस्तथा।
स्वर्गं दिवः समुद्रांश्च नदान् शैलान् वनस्पतीन् ॥68॥
1.6.m: Water, fire, earth, wind, the intermediate space, and the quarters, / heaven, the sky, the oceans, rivers, mountains, trees,

1.6.s:
oṣadhīnāṃ tathātmāno hyātmāno vṛkṣavīrudhām.
lavāḥ kāṣṭhāḥ kalāścaiva muhūrttāḥ sandhirātryahāḥ ..69..
1.6.d:
ओषधीनां तथात्मानो ह्यात्मानो वृक्षवीरुधाम्।
लवाः काष्ठाः कलाश्चैव मुहूर्त्ताः सन्धिरात्र्यहाः ॥69॥
1.6.m: the spirits of medicinal plants, and the spirits of trees and creeping vines; / *lava*s, *kāṣṭhā*s, *kalā*s, *muhūrta*s, twilight junctures, nights and days,

1.6.s:
arddhamāsāśca māsāśca ayanābdayugāni ca.
sthānābhimāninaḥ sarve sthānākhyāścaiva te smṛtāḥ ..70..
1.6.d:
अर्द्धमासाश्च मासाश्च अयनाब्दयुगानि च।
स्थानाभिमानिनः सर्वे स्थानाख्याश्चैव ते स्मृताः ॥70॥
1.6.m: half-months, months, solstitial courses, years, and *yuga*s. / All these are known as presiding deities of stations, and they bear the names of their respective stations.

1.6.s:
vakrādyasya brāhmaṇāḥ saṃprasūtāstadvakṣastaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pūrvabhāgaiḥ.
vaiśyāścorvoryasya padbhyāñca śūdrāḥ sarve varṇā gātrataḥ saṃprasūtāḥ ..71..
1.6.d:
वक्राद्यस्य ब्राह्मणाः संप्रसूतास्तद्वक्षस्तः क्षत्रियाः पूर्वभागैः।
वैश्याश्चोर्वोर्यस्य पद्भ्याञ्च शूद्राः सर्वे वर्णा गात्रतः संप्रसूताः ॥71॥
1.6.m: From his mouth the brāhmaṇas were produced; from his chest, the kṣatriyas, from its upper parts; / from his thighs the vaiśyas, and from his feet the śūdras: all classes were produced from his limbs.

1.6.s:
nārāyaṇaḥ paro'vyaktādaṇḍamavyaktasambhavam.
aṇḍājjajñe punarbrahmā lokāstena kṛtāḥ svayam ..72..
1.6.d:
नारायणः परोऽव्यक्तादण्डमव्यक्तसम्भवम्।
अण्डाज्जज्ञे पुनर्ब्रह्मा लोकास्तेन कृताः स्वयम् ॥72॥
1.6.m: Nārāyaṇa is beyond the unmanifest; from the unmanifest arose the egg. / From the egg Brahmā was born again; by him the worlds were made personally.

1.6.s:
eṣa vaḥ kathitaḥ pādaḥ samāsānna tu vistarāt.
anenādyena pādena purāṇaṃ saṃprakīrtitam ..73..
1.6.d:
एष वः कथितः पादः समासान्न तु विस्तरात्।
अनेनाद्येन पादेन पुराणं संप्रकीर्तितम् ॥73॥
1.6.m: This section has been told to you in summary, not in full detail. / Through this first section, the Purāṇa has been proclaimed.

1.6.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte sṛṣṭiprakaraṇaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭho'dhyāyaḥ .. 6 ..
1.6.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते सृष्टिप्रकरणं नाम षष्ठोऽध्यायः ॥ 6 ॥
1.6.m: Thus ends the sixth chapter, named 'The Topic of Creation', in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.6.s: samāptaḥ prakriyāpādaḥ ..
1.6.d: समाप्तः प्रक्रियापादः ॥
1.6.m: The Introductory Section (Prakriyāpāda) is completed.

1.7.s:
ityeṣa prathamaḥ pādaḥ prakriyārthaḥ prakīrtitaḥ.
śrutvā tu saṃhṛṣṭamanāḥ kāśyapeyaḥ sanātanaḥ ..1..
1.7.d:
इत्येष प्रथमः पादः प्रक्रियार्थः प्रकीर्तितः।
श्रुत्वा तु संहृष्टमनाः काश्यपेयः सनातनः ॥1॥
1.7.m: Thus this first section, whose subject is the introduction, has been proclaimed. / Having heard it, eternal Kāśyapeya, with a delighted heart,

1.7.s:
sambodhya sūtaṃ vacasā papracchāthottarāṃ kathām.
ataḥprabhṛti kalpajña pratisaṃdhiṃ pracakṣva naḥ ..2..
1.7.d:
सम्बोध्य सूतं वचसा पप्रच्छाथोत्तरां कथाम्।
अतःप्रभृति कल्पज्ञ प्रतिसंधिं प्रचक्ष्व नः ॥2॥
1.7.m: addressed the Sūta with words and then asked about the subsequent narration: / 'From here on, O knower of aeons, tell us about the transition between aeons,

1.7.s:
samatītasya kalpasya varttamānasya cobhayoḥ.
kalpayorantaraṃ yacca pratisaṃdhiryatastayoḥ.
etadveditumicchāmaḥ atyantakuśalo hyasi ..3..
1.7.d:
समतीतस्य कल्पस्य वर्त्तमानस्य चोभयोः।
कल्पयोरन्तरं यच्च प्रतिसंधिर्यतस्तयोः।
एतद्वेदितुमिच्छामः अत्यन्तकुशलो ह्यसि ॥3॥
1.7.m: between both the past aeon and the present one, / and the interval between the two aeons from which their transition arises. / This we desire to know, for you are exceedingly skilled.'

1.7.s: ..lomaharṣaṇa uvāca..
1.7.d: ॥लोमहर्षण उवाच॥
1.7.m:
Lomaharṣaṇa said:
Here I shall explain to you the transition between both of them,
the aeon that has passed and the one that is current.

1.7.s:
atra vo'haṃ pravakṣyāmi pratisaṃdhiñca yastayoḥ.
samatītasya kalpasya varttamānasya cobhayoḥ ..4..
1.7.d:
अत्र वोऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रतिसंधिञ्च यस्तयोः।
समतीतस्य कल्पस्य वर्त्तमानस्य चोभयोः ॥4॥

1.7.s:
manvantarāṇi kalpeṣu yeṣu yāni ca suvratāḥ.
yaścāyaṃ varttate kalpo vārāhaḥ sāmprataḥ śubhaḥ ..5..
1.7.d:
मन्वन्तराणि कल्पेषु येषु यानि च सुव्रताः।
यश्चायं वर्त्तते कल्पो वाराहः साम्प्रतः शुभः ॥5॥
1.7.m: and which cosmic ages of a Manu occur in those aeons, O men of good vows, / and this present auspicious aeon that is now current, the Vārāha.

1.7.s:
asmāt kalpācca yaḥ kalpaḥ pūrvo'tītaḥ sanātanaḥ.
tasya cāsya ca kalpasya madhyāvasthānnibodhata ..6..
1.7.d:
अस्मात् कल्पाच्च यः कल्पः पूर्वोऽतीतः सनातनः।
तस्य चास्य च कल्पस्य मध्यावस्थान्निबोधत ॥6॥
1.7.m: And the aeon that was before this aeon, the past eternal one— / understand from me the intermediate state between that aeon and this one.

1.7.s:
pratyāhṛte pūrvakalpe pratisaṃdhiṃ ca tatra vai.
anyaḥ pravarttate kalpo janāllokāt punaḥ punaḥ ..7..
1.7.d:
प्रत्याहृते पूर्वकल्पे प्रतिसंधिं च तत्र वै।
अन्यः प्रवर्त्तते कल्पो जनाल्लोकात् पुनः पुनः ॥7॥
1.7.m: When the previous aeon is withdrawn, and in that transition, indeed, / another aeon proceeds again and again from the Janaloka.

1.7.s:
vyucchinnāt pratisaṃdhestu kalpāt kalpaḥ parasparam.
vyucchidyante kriyāḥsarvāḥ kalpānte sarvaśastadā.
tasmāt kalpāttu kalpasya pratisaṃdhirnigadyate ..8..
1.7.d:
व्युच्छिन्नात् प्रतिसंधेस्तु कल्पात् कल्पः परस्परम्।
व्युच्छिद्यन्ते क्रियाःसर्वाः कल्पान्ते सर्वशस्तदा।
तस्मात् कल्पात्तु कल्पस्य प्रतिसंधिर्निगद्यते ॥8॥
1.7.m: From an aeon whose transition has been broken, one aeon after another [proceeds]. / At the end of an aeon all ritual acts are broken off entirely at that time; / therefore, the transition from aeon to aeon is declared.

1.7.s:
manvantarayugākhyānāmapyucchinnāśca sandhayaḥ.
parasparāḥ pravarttante manvantarayugaiḥ saha ..9..
1.7.d:
मन्वन्तरयुगाख्यानामप्युच्छिन्नाश्च सन्धयः।
परस्पराः प्रवर्त्तन्ते मन्वन्तरयुगैः सह ॥9॥
1.7.m: The transitions of what are called cosmic ages of a Manu and yugas, though broken off, / proceed mutually along with the cosmic ages of a Manu and the yugas.

1.7.s:
uktā ye prakriyārthena pūrvakalpāḥ samāsataḥ.
teṣāṃ parārddhakalpānāṃ pūrvo hyasmāttu yaḥ paraḥ.
āsīt kalpo vyatīto vai parārddhena parastu saḥ ..10..
1.7.d:
उक्ता ये प्रक्रियार्थेन पूर्वकल्पाः समासतः।
तेषां परार्द्धकल्पानां पूर्वो ह्यस्मात्तु यः परः।
आसीत् कल्पो व्यतीतो वै परार्द्धेन परस्तु सः ॥10॥
1.7.m: The past aeons that were mentioned in summary for the purpose of the introduction— / of those aeons of the first half, the one prior to this present one, / that past aeon, was the last of the first half.

1.7.s:
anye bhaviṣyā ye kalpā aparārddhādguṇīkṛtāḥ.
prathamaḥ sāmpratasteṣāṃ kalpo'yaṃ varttate dvijāḥ ..11..
1.7.d:
अन्ये भविष्या ये कल्पा अपरार्द्धाद्गुणीकृताः।
प्रथमः साम्प्रतस्तेषां कल्पोऽयं वर्त्तते द्विजाः ॥11॥
1.7.m: The other aeons that are to come, multiplied from the second half— / among them, this present aeon that is now current is the first, O twice-born.

1.7.s:
yasmin pūrvaḥ parārddhe tu dvitīye para ucyate.
etāvān sthitikālaśca pratyāhārastataḥ smṛtaḥ ..12..
1.7.d:
यस्मिन् पूर्वः परार्द्धे तु द्वितीये पर उच्यते।
एतावान् स्थितिकालश्च प्रत्याहारस्ततः स्मृतः ॥12॥
1.7.m: The former is said to be in the first half, while the latter is in the second. / Such is the duration of maintenance, and the withdrawal thereafter is remembered.

1.7.s:
asmāt kalpāttu yaḥ pūrvaṃ kalpo'tītaḥ sanātanaḥ.
caturyugasahasrānte aho manvantaraiḥ purā ..13..
1.7.d:
अस्मात् कल्पात्तु यः पूर्वं कल्पोऽतीतः सनातनः।
चतुर्युगसहस्रान्ते अहो मन्वन्तरैः पुरा ॥13॥
1.7.m: The eternal aeon that was prior to this aeon, / at the end of a thousand four-yuga cycles, in the ancient past, with its day of cosmic ages of Manus—

1.7.s:
kṣīṇe kalpe tadā tasmin dāhakāle hyupasthite.
tasmin kalpe tadā devā āsanvaimānikāstu ye ..14..
1.7.d:
क्षीणे कल्पे तदा तस्मिन् दाहकाले ह्युपस्थिते।
तस्मिन् कल्पे तदा देवा आसन्वैमानिकास्तु ये ॥14॥
1.7.m: when that aeon was exhausted at that time, and the time of conflagration had arrived, / the gods who dwelled in aerial cars in that aeon at that time,

1.7.s:
nakṣatragrahatārāstu candrasūryagrahāśca ye.
aṣṭāviṃśatirevaitāḥ koṭyastu sukṛtātmanām ..15..
1.7.d:
नक्षत्रग्रहतारास्तु चन्द्रसूर्यग्रहाश्च ये।
अष्टाविंशतिरेवैताः कोट्यस्तु सुकृतात्मनाम् ॥15॥
1.7.m: and the constellations, planets, stars, and the moon and sun— / these were twenty-eight crores of souls of meritorious deeds.

1.7.s:
manvantare tathaikasmin caturdaśasu vai tathā.
trīṇi koṭiśatānyāsan koṭyādvinavatistathā.
aṣṭādhikāḥ saptaśatāḥ sahasrāṇāṃ smṛtāḥ purā ..16..
1.7.d:
मन्वन्तरे तथैकस्मिन् चतुर्दशसु वै तथा।
त्रीणि कोटिशतान्यासन् कोट्याद्विनवतिस्तथा।
अष्टाधिकाः सप्तशताः सहस्राणां स्मृताः पुरा ॥16॥
1.7.m: In one cosmic age of a Manu and likewise across the fourteen, / there were three hundred crores, and ninety-two crores, / and seven hundred and eight thousands remembered in the past,

1.7.s:
vaimānikānāṃ devānāṃ kalpe'tīte tu ye'bhavan.
ekaikasmiṃstu kalpe vai devā vaimānikāḥ smṛtāḥ ..17..
1.7.d:
वैमानिकानां देवानां कल्पेऽतीते तु येऽभवन्।
एकैकस्मिंस्तु कल्पे वै देवा वैमानिकाः स्मृताः ॥17॥
1.7.m: of gods dwelling in aerial cars who existed in the past aeon. / In each single aeon, gods dwelling in aerial cars are recorded.

1.7.s:
atha manvantareṣvāsaṃścaturdaśasu vai divi.
devāśca pitaraścaiva munayo manavastathā ..18..
1.7.d:
अथ मन्वन्तरेष्वासंश्चतुर्दशसु वै दिवि।
देवाश्च पितरश्चैव मुनयो मनवस्तथा ॥18॥
1.7.m: Then, in the fourteen cosmic ages of a Manu, there were in heaven / gods and ancestors, seers, and Manus,

1.7.s:
teṣāmanucarā ye ca manuputrāstathaiva ca.
varṇāśramibhirīḍyāśca tasmin kāle tu ye surāḥ.
manvantareṣu yehyāsan devaloke divaukasaḥ ..19..
1.7.d:
तेषामनुचरा ये च मनुपुत्रास्तथैव च।
वर्णाश्रमिभिरीड्याश्च तस्मिन् काले तु ये सुराः।
मन्वन्तरेषु येह्यासन् देवलोके दिवौकसः ॥19॥
1.7.m: and their attendants, and likewise the sons of Manus, / and the gods at that time who were worshipful to members of the classes and stages of life, / who were the heaven-dwellers in the world of the gods during the cosmic ages of a Manu.

1.7.s:
te taiḥ saṃyojakaiḥ sārddhaṃ prāpte saṅkalane tathā.
tulyaniṣṭhāstu te sarve prāpte hyābhūtasaṃplave ..20..
1.7.d:
ते तैः संयोजकैः सार्द्धं प्राप्ते सङ्कलने तथा।
तुल्यनिष्ठास्तु ते सर्वे प्राप्ते ह्याभूतसंप्लवे ॥20॥
1.7.m: Together with those unifiers, when the time of gathering arrived, / they all possessed equal status when the cosmic dissolution arrived.

1.7.s:
tataste'vaśyabhāvitvād buddhvā paryāyamātmanaḥ.
trailokyavāsino devāstasmin prāpte hyupaplave ..21..
1.7.d:
ततस्तेऽवश्यभावित्वाद् बुद्ध्वा पर्यायमात्मनः।
त्रैलोक्यवासिनो देवास्तस्मिन् प्राप्ते ह्युपप्लवे ॥21॥
1.7.m: Then, knowing their own turn of destiny due to its inevitability, / the gods residing in the three worlds, when that calamity arrived,

1.7.s:
te'nautsukyaviṣādena tyaktvā sthānāni bhāvataḥ.
maharllokāya saṃvignāstataste dadhire matim ..22..
1.7.d:
तेऽनौत्सुक्यविषादेन त्यक्त्वा स्थानानि भावतः।
महर्ल्लोकाय संविग्नास्ततस्ते दधिरे मतिम् ॥22॥
1.7.m: relinquishing their stations in reality without zeal and with dejection, / distressed, directed their minds toward Maharloka.

1.7.s:
te yuktā upapadyante mahasisthaiḥ śarīrakaiḥ.
viśuddhibahulāḥ sarve mānasīṃ siddhimāsthitāḥ ..23..
1.7.d:
ते युक्ता उपपद्यन्ते महसिस्थैः शरीरकैः।
विशुद्धिबहुलाः सर्वे मानसीं सिद्धिमास्थिताः ॥23॥
1.7.m: Absorbed in meditation, they are reborn there with bodies suited to Maharloka, / all possessing abundant purity, having attained mental accomplishment,

1.7.s:
taiḥ kalpa vāsibhiḥ sārddhaṃ mahānāsāditastu yaiḥ.
brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyairvaiśyaistadbhaktaiścāparairjjanaiḥ ..24..
1.7.d:
तैः कल्प वासिभिः सार्द्धं महानासादितस्तु यैः।
ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यैस्तद्भक्तैश्चापरैर्ज्जनैः ॥24॥
1.7.m: together with those aeon-dwellers by whom Mahas had been attained— / brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and other people devoted to them.

1.7.s:
matvā tu te maharllokaṃ devasaṅghāścaturddaśa.
tataste janalokāya so dvegā dadhire matim ..25..
1.7.d:
मत्वा तु ते महर्ल्लोकं देवसङ्घाश्चतुर्द्दश।
ततस्ते जनलोकाय सो द्वेगा दधिरे मतिम् ॥25॥
1.7.m: Having reflected on Maharloka, the fourteen hosts of gods / then agitatedly directed their minds toward Janaloka.

1.7.s:
viśuddhibahulāḥ sarve mānasīṃ siddhimāsthitāḥ.
taiḥ kalpavāsibhiḥ sāṃrddha mahānāsāditastu yaiḥ ..26..
1.7.d:
विशुद्धिबहुलाः सर्वे मानसीं सिद्धिमास्थिताः।
तैः कल्पवासिभिः सांर्द्ध महानासादितस्तु यैः ॥26॥
1.7.m: All possessing abundant purity, having attained mental accomplishment, / together with those aeon-dwellers by whom the Great [world] had been attained,

1.7.s:
daśakṛtva ivāvṛttyā tasmādgacchanti svastapaḥ.
tatra kalpān daśasthitvā satyaṃ gacchanti vai punaḥ.
etena kramayogena yānti kalpanivāsinaḥ ..27..
1.7.d:
दशकृत्व इवावृत्त्या तस्माद्गच्छन्ति स्वस्तपः।
तत्र कल्पान् दशस्थित्वा सत्यं गच्छन्ति वै पुनः।
एतेन क्रमयोगेन यान्ति कल्पनिवासिनः ॥27॥
1.7.m: revolving as if ten times, from there they go to Tapoloka. / Having stayed there for ten aeons, they go again to Satyaloka. / By this orderly sequence, the residents of the aeon proceed.

1.7.s:
evaṃ devayugānāntu sahasrāṇi parasparāt.
gatāni brahmalokaṃ vai aparāvarttinīṃ gatim ..28..
1.7.d:
एवं देवयुगानान्तु सहस्राणि परस्परात्।
गतानि ब्रह्मलोकं वै अपरावर्त्तिनीं गतिम् ॥28॥
1.7.m: Thus thousands of divine yugas have sequentially / gone to Brahmaloka, a state from which there is no return.

1.7.s:
ādhipatyaṃ vinā te vai aiśvaryeṇa tu tatsamāḥ.
bhavanti brahmaṇastulyā rūpeṇa viṣayeṇa ca ..29..
1.7.d:
आधिपत्यं विना ते वै ऐश्वर्येण तु तत्समाः।
भवन्ति ब्रह्मणस्तुल्या रूपेण विषयेण च ॥29॥
1.7.m: Without sovereignty, they are equal to him in sovereign power; / they become equal to Brahmā in form and in domain.

1.7.s:
tatra te hyavatiṣṭhanti prītiyuktāḥ prasaṅgamāt.
ānandaṃ brahmaṇaḥ prāpya mucyante brahmaṇā saha ..30..
1.7.d:
तत्र ते ह्यवतिष्ठन्ति प्रीतियुक्ताः प्रसङ्गमात्।
आनन्दं ब्रह्मणः प्राप्य मुच्यन्ते ब्रह्मणा सह ॥30॥
1.7.m: There they dwell filled with joy merely through association; / having attained the bliss of Brahmā, they are liberated along with Brahmā.

1.7.s:
avaśyambhāvinā'rthena prākṛtenaiva te svayam.
nānā tvenābhisambaddhāstadā tatkālabhāvinaḥ ..31..
1.7.d:
अवश्यम्भाविनाऽर्थेन प्राकृतेनैव ते स्वयम्।
नाना त्वेनाभिसम्बद्धास्तदा तत्कालभाविनः ॥31॥
1.7.m: By inevitable necessity, arising from primal matter itself, / they are personally connected with diversity, existing at that time.

1.7.s:
svarūpato buddhipūrvaṃ yathā bhavati jāgrataḥ.
tatkālabhāvi teṣāṃ tu tathā jñānaṃ pravarttate ..32..
1.7.d:
स्वरूपतो बुद्धिपूर्वं यथा भवति जाग्रतः।
तत्कालभावि तेषां तु तथा ज्ञानं प्रवर्त्तते ॥32॥
1.7.m: Just as in one awake knowledge arises deliberately according to one's true nature, / so their knowledge appropriate to that time operates.

1.7.s:
pratyāhāre tu bhedānāṃ yeṣāṃ bhinnābhisūṣmaṇām.
taiḥ sārddhaṃ pratisṛjyante kāryāṇi karaṇāni ca ..33..
1.7.d:
प्रत्याहारे तु भेदानां येषां भिन्नाभिसूष्मणाम्।
तैः सार्द्धं प्रतिसृज्यन्ते कार्याणि करणानि च ॥33॥
1.7.m: At the dissolution of distinct entities, for those whose subtle elements are dissolved, / along with them, effects and instruments are dissolved.

1.7.s:
nānātvadarśanātteṣāṃ brahmalokanivāsinām.
vinaṣṭasvādhikārāṇāṃ svena dharmeṇa tiṣṭhatām ..34..
1.7.d:
नानात्वदर्शनात्तेषां ब्रह्मलोकनिवासिनाम्।
विनष्टस्वाधिकाराणां स्वेन धर्मेण तिष्ठताम् ॥34॥
1.7.m: Because of their perception of diversity, for those dwellers in Brahmaloka / whose offices have perished, who abide in their own nature,

1.7.s:
te tulyalakṣaṇāḥ siddhāḥ śuddhātmāno nirañjanāḥ.
prakṛtau kāraṇātītāḥ svātmanyeva vyavasthitāḥ ..35..
1.7.d:
ते तुल्यलक्षणाः सिद्धाः शुद्धात्मानो निरञ्जनाः।
प्रकृतौ कारणातीताः स्वात्मन्येव व्यवस्थिताः ॥35॥
1.7.m: those accomplished ones of identical characteristics, pure-souled and taintless, / transcending causes in primal matter, abide only in the self.

1.7.s:
prakhyāpayitvā hyātmānaṃ prakṛtisteṣu sarvaśaḥ.
puruṣāvyavahṛtatvena pratītā na pravarttate ..36..
1.7.d:
प्रख्यापयित्वा ह्यात्मानं प्रकृतिस्तेषु सर्वशः।
पुरुषाव्यवहृतत्वेन प्रतीता न प्रवर्त्तते ॥36॥
1.7.m: Having revealed itself in every way, primal matter, / recognized as no longer serving any purpose for the spirit, ceases to operate toward them.

1.7.s:
pravartite punaḥ sarge teṣāṃ vā kāraṇaṃ punaḥ.
saṃyoge prākṛte teṣāṃ yuktānāṃ tattvadarśinām ..37..
1.7.d:
प्रवर्तिते पुनः सर्गे तेषां वा कारणं पुनः।
संयोगे प्राकृते तेषां युक्तानां तत्त्वदर्शिनाम् ॥37॥
1.7.m: When creation proceeds again, is there any cause again for them, / for those steadfast perceivers of reality, in the material union?

1.7.s:
atrāpavargiṇāṃ teṣāmapunarmārgagāminām.
abhāvaḥ punarutpattau śāntānāmarcciṣāmiva ..38..
1.7.d:
अत्रापवर्गिणां तेषामपुनर्मार्गगामिनाम्।
अभावः पुनरुत्पत्तौ शान्तानामर्च्चिषामिव ॥38॥
1.7.m: For those who have attained emancipation here, who travel on the path of no return, / there is non-existence regarding rebirth, like flames that have been extinguished.

1.7.s:
tatasteṣu gateṣūrddhvaṃ trailokyātsumahātmasu.
taiḥ sārddhaṃ ye maharllokāttadā nāsāditā janāḥ.
tacchiṣṭāśceha tiṣṭhanti kalpāddehamupāsate ..39..
1.7.d:
ततस्तेषु गतेषूर्द्ध्वं त्रैलोक्यात्सुमहात्मसु।
तैः सार्द्धं ये महर्ल्लोकात्तदा नासादिता जनाः।
तच्छिष्टाश्चेह तिष्ठन्ति कल्पाद्देहमुपासते ॥39॥
1.7.m: Then, when those great-souled beings had gone upward from the three worlds, / those people who had not reached [Janaloka] together with them from Maharloka / remained here as the remnants, and attend to their bodies from the beginning of the aeon:

1.7.s:
gandharvādyāḥ piśācāntā mānuṣā brāhmaṇādayaḥ.
paśavaḥ pakṣiṇaścaiva sthāvarāḥ sasarīsṛpāḥ ..40..
1.7.d:
गन्धर्वाद्याः पिशाचान्ता मानुषा ब्राह्मणादयः।
पशवः पक्षिणश्चैव स्थावराः ससरीसृपाः ॥40॥
1.7.m: [beings] beginning with the gandharvas and ending with the piśācas, humans beginning with the brāhmaṇas, / animals, birds, immobile things, and reptiles.

1.7.s:
tiṣṭhatsu teṣu tatkālaṃ pṛthivītalavāsiṣu.
sahasraṃ yattu raśmīnāṃ sūryasyeha vibhāsate.
te saptaraśmayo bhūtvā hyekaiko jāyate raviḥ ..41..
1.7.d:
तिष्ठत्सु तेषु तत्कालं पृथिवीतलवासिषु।
सहस्रं यत्तु रश्मीनां सूर्यस्येह विभासते।
ते सप्तरश्मयो भूत्वा ह्येकैको जायते रविः ॥41॥
1.7.m: While those dwellers on the surface of the earth remained at that time, / the thousand rays of the sun that shine here / became seven rays, and each became a sun.

1.7.s:
krameṇottiṣṭhamānāste trīn lokān pradahantyuta.
jaṅgamāḥ sthāvarāḥ caiva nadīḥ saṃrvāśca parvatān.
pūrve śuṣkā hyanāvṛṣṭyā sūryaistaiśca pradhūpitāḥ ..42..
1.7.d:
क्रमेणोत्तिष्ठमानास्ते त्रीन् लोकान् प्रदहन्त्युत।
जङ्गमाः स्थावराः चैव नदीः संर्वाश्च पर्वतान्।
पूर्वे शुष्का ह्यनावृष्ट्या सूर्यैस्तैश्च प्रधूपिताः ॥42॥
1.7.m: Rising in succession, they burn up the three worlds— / moving and immobile things, all rivers and mountains— / dried up previously by drought and scorched by those suns.

1.7.s:
tadā te viviśuḥ sarve nirddagdhāḥ sūryaraśmibhiḥ.
jaṅgamāḥ sthāvarāḥ sarve dharmādharmātmakāstu vai ..43..
1.7.d:
तदा ते विविशुः सर्वे निर्द्दग्धाः सूर्यरश्मिभिः।
जङ्गमाः स्थावराः सर्वे धर्माधर्मात्मकास्तु वै ॥43॥
1.7.m: Then they all, burned completely by the sun's rays, entered [destruction]— / all moving and immobile beings, comprised of virtue and vice.

1.7.s:
dagdhadehāstataste vai gatāḥ pāpayugātyaye.
yonyā tayā hyanirmuktāḥ śubhapāpānubandhayā ..44..
1.7.d:
दग्धदेहास्ततस्ते वै गताः पापयुगात्यये।
योन्या तया ह्यनिर्मुक्ताः शुभपापानुबन्धया ॥44॥
1.7.m: Their bodies burned, they went, at the end of the sinful yuga, / not yet freed from that womb bound to good and evil.

1.7.s:
tataste hyupapadyante tulyarūpā jane janāḥ.
viśuddhibahulāḥ sarve mānasīṃ siddhimāsthitāḥ ..45..
1.7.d:
ततस्ते ह्युपपद्यन्ते तुल्यरूपा जने जनाः।
विशुद्धिबहुलाः सर्वे मानसीं सिद्धिमास्थिताः ॥45॥
1.7.m: Then, in Janaloka, those people are born with similar forms, / full of purity, all having attained mental perfection.

1.7.s:
uṣitvā rajanīṃ tatra brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ.
punaḥ sarge bhavantīha brahmaṇo mānasīprajāḥ ..46..
1.7.d:
उषित्वा रजनीं तत्र ब्रह्मणोऽव्यक्तजन्मनः।
पुनः सर्गे भवन्तीह ब्रह्मणो मानसीप्रजाः ॥46॥
1.7.m: Having dwelt there for the night of Brahmā, whose birth is unmanifest, / at the recreation they become here the mind-born offspring of Brahmā.

1.7.s:
tatasteṣu pravṛtteṣu jane trailokyavāsiṣu.
nirdagdheṣu ca lokeṣu teṣu sūryaistu saptabhiḥ.
vṛṣṭyā kṣitau plāvitāyāṃ viśīrṇeṣvālayeṣu ca ..47..
1.7.d:
ततस्तेषु प्रवृत्तेषु जने त्रैलोक्यवासिषु।
निर्दग्धेषु च लोकेषु तेषु सूर्यैस्तु सप्तभिः।
वृष्ट्या क्षितौ प्लावितायां विशीर्णेष्वालयेषु च ॥47॥
1.7.m: Then, when those dwellers of the three worlds had gone to Janaloka, / and when those worlds were burned up by the seven suns, / the earth was flooded with rain, and dwellings were shattered.

1.7.s:
samudrāścaiva meghāśca āpaḥ sarvāśca pārthivāḥ.
vrajantyekārṇavatvaṃ hi salilākhyāstadāśritāḥ ..48..
1.7.d:
समुद्राश्चैव मेघाश्च आपः सर्वाश्च पार्थिवाः।
व्रजन्त्येकार्णवत्वं हि सलिलाख्यास्तदाश्रिताः ॥48॥
1.7.m: Oceans, clouds, and all earthly waters, / taking recourse to them, attain the state of a single ocean, known as water.

1.7.s:
āgatāgatikaṃ tadvai yadā tu salilaṃ bahu.
saṃchādyemāṃ sthitāṃ bhūmimarṇavākhyā tadā ca sā ..49..
1.7.d:
आगतागतिकं तद्वै यदा तु सलिलं बहु।
संछाद्येमां स्थितां भूमिमर्णवाख्या तदा च सा ॥49॥
1.7.m: When that abundant water, whose course is ceaseless, / remains covering this earth, it is called an ocean (arṇava).

1.7.s:
ābhāti yasmānnābhānti bhāsanto vyāptidīptiṣu.
sarvataḥ samanuplāvya tāsāñcāmbho vibhāvyate ..50..
1.7.d:
आभाति यस्मान्नाभान्ति भासन्तो व्याप्तिदीप्तिषु।
सर्वतः समनुप्लाव्य तासाञ्चाम्भो विभाव्यते ॥50॥
1.7.m: Since [the lights] do not shine where it spreads, although shining with pervasion and brilliance, / inundating all around, the water of these [lights] is perceived.

1.7.s:
tadambhastanute yasmāt sarvāṃ pṛthvīṃ samantataḥ.
dhātustanotirvistāre tenāmbhastanavaḥ smṛtāḥ ..51..
1.7.d:
तदम्भस्तनुते यस्मात् सर्वां पृथ्वीं समन्ततः।
धातुस्तनोतिर्विस्तारे तेनाम्भस्तनवः स्मृताः ॥51॥
1.7.m: Because that water (ambhas) spreads (tanute) all over the earth entirely— / the verbal root tan- means extension—therefore waters are remembered as bodies (tanu).

1.7.s:
aramityeṣa śīghrantu nipātaḥ kavibhiḥ smṛtaḥ.
ekārṇave bhavantyāpo na śīghrāstena te narāḥ ..52..
1.7.d:
अरमित्येष शीघ्रन्तु निपातः कविभिः स्मृतः।
एकार्णवे भवन्त्यापो न शीघ्रास्तेन ते नराः ॥52॥
1.7.m: ‘Aram’ is remembered by poets as an indeclinable meaning ‘swiftly’; / in the single ocean the waters become not swift (na-ara), hence they are called nārāḥ.

1.7.s:
tasmin yugasahasrānte saṃsthite brahmaṇo'hani.
rājanyāṃ varttamānāyāntāvattat salilātmanā ..53..
1.7.d:
तस्मिन् युगसहस्रान्ते संस्थिते ब्रह्मणोऽहनि।
राजन्यां वर्त्तमानायान्तावत्तत् सलिलात्मना ॥53॥
1.7.m: At that end of a thousand yugas, when the day of Brahmā has ended, / and the night is proceeding, it remains as water for that long.

1.7.s:
tatastu salile tasminnaṣṭe'gnau pṛthivītale.
praśāntavāte'ndhakāre nirāloke samantataḥ ..54..
1.7.d:
ततस्तु सलिले तस्मिन्नष्टेऽग्नौ पृथिवीतले।
प्रशान्तवातेऽन्धकारे निरालोके समन्ततः ॥54॥
1.7.m: Then, in that water, when fire had perished on the surface of the earth, / the wind had ceased, and darkness was without light all around,

1.7.s:
yenaivādhiṣṭhitaṃ hīdaṃ brahmā sa puruṣaḥ prabhuḥ.
vibhāgamasya lokasya punarvai kartumicchati ..55..
1.7.d:
येनैवाधिष्ठितं हीदं ब्रह्मा स पुरुषः प्रभुः।
विभागमस्य लोकस्य पुनर्वै कर्तुमिच्छति ॥55॥
1.7.m: that Lord Brahmā, the Puruṣa by whom this is presided over, / desires to make the division of this world again.

1.7.s:
ekārṇave tadā tasminnaṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame.
tadā sa bhavati brahmā sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt ..56..
1.7.d:
एकार्णवे तदा तस्मिन्नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे।
तदा स भवति ब्रह्मा सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात् ॥56॥
1.7.m: Then, in that single ocean, when moving and immobile things had perished, / Brahmā became the one with a thousand eyes and a thousand feet,

1.7.s:
sahasraśīrṣā puruṣo rukmavarṇo hyatīndriyaḥ.
brahmā nārāyaṇākhyastu suṣvāpa salile tadā ..57..
1.7.d:
सहस्रशीर्षा पुरुषो रुक्मवर्णो ह्यतीन्द्रियः।
ब्रह्मा नारायणाख्यस्तु सुष्वाप सलिले तदा ॥57॥
1.7.m: the thousand-headed Puruṣa, golden-hued and beyond the senses; / Brahmā, named Nārāyaṇa, then slept upon the water.

1.7.s:
sattvodrekāt prabuddhastu śūnyaṃ lokamavekṣya ca.
imañcodāharantyatra ślokaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prati ..58..
1.7.d:
सत्त्वोद्रेकात् प्रबुद्धस्तु शून्यं लोकमवेक्ष्य च।
इमञ्चोदाहरन्त्यत्र श्लोकं नारायणं प्रति ॥58॥
1.7.m: Awakened by an excess of sattva and beholding an empty world— / here they cite this verse concerning Nārāyaṇa:

1.7.s:
āpo nārākhyāstanava ityapānnāma śuśrumaḥ.
āpūrya nābhiṃ tatrāste tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ..59..
1.7.d:
आपो नाराख्यास्तनव इत्यपान्नाम शुश्रुमः।
आपूर्य नाभिं तत्रास्ते तेन नारायणः स्मृतः ॥59॥
1.7.m: ‘Waters are the bodies named nārāḥ: this we have heard as the name of the waters. / Having filled [them], he lies with them as his resting-place (ayana); therefore he is remembered as Nārāyaṇa.’

1.7.s:
sahasraśīrṣā sumanāḥ sahasrapāt sahasracakṣurvadanaḥ sahasrabhuk.
sahasrabāhuḥ prathamaḥ prajā patistrayīpathe yaḥ puruṣo nirucyate ..60..
1.7.d:
सहस्रशीर्षा सुमनाः सहस्रपात् सहस्रचक्षुर्वदनः सहस्रभुक्।
सहस्रबाहुः प्रथमः प्रजा पतिस्त्रयीपथे यः पुरुषो निरुच्यते ॥60॥
1.7.m: He who is described in the path of the three Vedas as the thousand-headed, benevolent, thousand-footed, thousand-eyed, thousand-faced, thousand-eating, / thousand-armed, first Prajāpati, the Puruṣa,

1.7.s:
ādityavarṇo bhuvanasya goptā eko hyapūrvaḥ prathamaṃ turāṣāṭ.
hiraṇyagarbhaḥ puruṣo mahātmā sa paṭhyate vai tamasaḥparastāt ..61..
1.7.d:
आदित्यवर्णो भुवनस्य गोप्ता एको ह्यपूर्वः प्रथमं तुराषाट्।
हिरण्यगर्भः पुरुषो महात्मा स पठ्यते वै तमसःपरस्तात् ॥61॥
1.7.m: sun-coloured, guardian of the world, single, without precedent, the foremost conqueror of the mighty, / Hiraṇyagarbha, the great-souled Puruṣa, is recited as being beyond darkness.

1.7.s:
kalpādau rajasodrikto brahmā bhūtvā'sṛjat prajāḥ.
kalpānte tamasodrikto kālo bhūtvā'grasat punaḥ ..62..
1.7.d:
कल्पादौ रजसोद्रिक्तो ब्रह्मा भूत्वाऽसृजत् प्रजाः।
कल्पान्ते तमसोद्रिक्तो कालो भूत्वाऽग्रसत् पुनः ॥62॥
1.7.m: At the beginning of an aeon, swollen with rajas, having become Brahmā he created beings; / at the end of an aeon, swollen with tamas, having become Time he swallowed them again.

1.7.s:
sa vai nārāyaṇā khyastu sattvodrikto'rṇave svapan.
tridhā vibhajya cātmānaṃ trailokye samavarttata ..63..
1.7.d:
स वै नारायणा ख्यस्तु सत्त्वोद्रिक्तोऽर्णवे स्वपन्।
त्रिधा विभज्य चात्मानं त्रैलोक्ये समवर्त्तत ॥63॥
1.7.m: Named Nārāyaṇa, swollen with sattva, sleeping in the ocean, / dividing himself threefold, he operated in the three worlds.

1.7.s:
sṛjate grasate caiva vīkṣante ca tribhistu tān.
ekārṇave tadā loke naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame ..64..
1.7.d:
सृजते ग्रसते चैव वीक्षन्ते च त्रिभिस्तु तान्।
एकार्णवे तदा लोके नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे ॥64॥
1.7.m: He creates, swallows, and watches them through the three [forms], / when the world was a single ocean and moving and immobile things had perished.

1.7.s:
caturyugasahasrānte sarvataḥ salilāvṛte.
brahmā nārāyaṇākhyastu aprakāśārṇave svapan ..65..
1.7.d:
चतुर्युगसहस्रान्ते सर्वतः सलिलावृते।
ब्रह्मा नारायणाख्यस्तु अप्रकाशार्णवे स्वपन् ॥65॥
1.7.m: At the end of a thousand four-yuga cycles, when all was covered with water, / Brahmā, named Nārāyaṇa, sleeping in the unillumined ocean,

1.7.s:
caturvidhāḥ prajā grastvā brāhmyāṃ rātryāṃ mahārṇave.
paśyanti taṃ maharllokāt suptaṃ kālaṃ maharṣayaḥ ..66..
1.7.d:
चतुर्विधाः प्रजा ग्रस्त्वा ब्राह्म्यां रात्र्यां महार्णवे।
पश्यन्ति तं महर्ल्लोकात् सुप्तं कालं महर्षयः ॥66॥
1.7.m: having swallowed the four kinds of beings during Brahmā's night in the great ocean, / is seen by the great seers from Maharloka as Time asleep.

1.7.s:
bhṛgvādayo yathā sapta kalpe hyasmin maharṣayaḥ.
tato vivarttamānaistairmahān parigataḥ paraḥ ..67..
1.7.d:
भृग्वादयो यथा सप्त कल्पे ह्यस्मिन् महर्षयः।
ततो विवर्त्तमानैस्तैर्महान् परिगतः परः ॥67॥
1.7.m: Just as in this aeon there are the seven great seers beginning with Bhṛgu, / then by them revolving there the supreme, great [Lord] was perceived.

1.7.s:
gatyarthād ṛṣayo dhātornnāmanirvṛttirāditaḥ.
tasmādṛṣiparatvena mahāṃstasmānmaharṣayaḥ ..68..
1.7.d:
गत्यर्थाद् ऋषयो धातोर्न्नामनिर्वृत्तिरादितः।
तस्मादृषिपरत्वेन महांस्तस्मान्महर्षयः ॥68॥
1.7.m: From the verbal root meaning ‘movement’ the name ‘ṛṣi’ was formed in the beginning; / because he is beyond the seers, he is the great one, therefore they are great seers.

1.7.s:
maharllokasthitairdṛṣṭaḥ kālaḥ suptastadā ca taiḥ.
satyādyāḥ sapta yehyāsan kalpe'tīte maharṣayaḥ ..69..
1.7.d:
महर्ल्लोकस्थितैर्दृष्टः कालः सुप्तस्तदा च तैः।
सत्याद्याः सप्त येह्यासन् कल्पेऽतीते महर्षयः ॥69॥
1.7.m: Time was seen asleep then by those who stood in Maharloka, / the seven great seers beginning with Satya who existed in the past aeon.

1.7.s:
evaṃ brāhmīṣu rātrīṣu hyatī tāsu sahasraśaḥ.
dṛṣṭavantastathā hyanye suptaṃ kālaṃ maharṣayaḥ ..70..
1.7.d:
एवं ब्राह्मीषु रात्रीषु ह्यती तासु सहस्रशः।
दृष्टवन्तस्तथा ह्यन्ये सुप्तं कालं महर्षयः ॥70॥
1.7.m: Thus, when thousands of nights of Brahmā had passed away, / other great seers likewise have seen Time asleep.

1.7.s: kalpayāmāsa vai brahmā tasmāt kālo nirucyate ..71..
1.7.d: कल्पयामास वै ब्रह्मा तस्मात् कालो निरुच्यते ॥71॥
1.7.m: Brahmā ordered (kalpayāmāsa) [it], and therefore he is called Time (kāla).

1.7.s:
sa sraṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ kalpādiṣu punaḥ punaḥ.
vyaktāvyakto mahādevastasya sarvamidaṃ jagat ..72..
1.7.d:
स स्रष्टा सर्वभूतानां कल्पादिषु पुनः पुनः।
व्यक्ताव्यक्तो महादेवस्तस्य सर्वमिदं जगत् ॥72॥
1.7.m: He is the creator of all beings at the beginnings of aeons again and again, / Mahādeva, manifest and unmanifest; to him belongs this whole universe.

1.7.s:
ityeṣa pratisandhirvaḥ kīrttitaḥ kalpayordvayoḥ.
sāmpratātītayormadhye prāgavasthā babhūva yā ..73..
1.7.d:
इत्येष प्रतिसन्धिर्वः कीर्त्तितः कल्पयोर्द्वयोः।
साम्प्रतातीतयोर्मध्ये प्रागवस्था बभूव या ॥73॥
1.7.m: Thus this transition between two aeons has been proclaimed to you, / which occurred as the prior state between the present and the past [aeons].

1.7.s:
kīrttitā tu samāsena kalpe kalpe yathā tathā.
sāmprataṃ te pravakṣyāmi kalpametaṃ nibodhata ..74..
1.7.d:
कीर्त्तिता तु समासेन कल्पे कल्पे यथा तथा।
साम्प्रतं ते प्रवक्ष्यामि कल्पमेतं निबोधत ॥74॥
1.7.m: It has been proclaimed in brief, as it occurs in aeon after aeon; / now I shall tell you of this present aeon; learn of it.

1.7.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte pratisandhikīrttanaṃ nāma saptamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 7 ..
1.7.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते प्रतिसन्धिकीर्त्तनं नाम सप्तमोऽध्यायः ॥ 7 ॥
1.7.m: Thus ends the seventh chapter, named ‘Account of the Transition [Between Aeons]’, in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.8.s: ..sūta uvāca..
1.8.d: ॥सूत उवाच॥
1.8.m:
The Sūta said:
Having waited out the time of night, equal to a thousand yugas,
at the end of the night he assumes the state of Brahmā for the sake of creation.

1.8.s:
tulyaṃ yugasahasrasya naiśaṃ kālamupāsya saḥ.
śarvaryante prakurute brahmatvaṃ sargakāraṇāt ..1..
1.8.d:
तुल्यं युगसहस्रस्य नैशं कालमुपास्य सः।
शर्वर्यन्ते प्रकुरुते ब्रह्मत्वं सर्गकारणात् ॥1॥

1.8.s:
brahmā tu salile tasmin vāyurbhūtvā tadācarat.
andhakāre tadā tasmin naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame ..2..
1.8.d:
ब्रह्मा तु सलिले तस्मिन् वायुर्भूत्वा तदाचरत्।
अन्धकारे तदा तस्मिन् नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे ॥2॥
1.8.m: Brahmā moved about in that water, having become the wind, / in that darkness, when moving and immobile things had perished,

1.8.s:
jalena samanuvyāpte sarvataḥ pṛthivītale.
avibhāgena bhūteṣu samantātsusthiteṣu ca ..3..
1.8.d:
जलेन समनुव्याप्ते सर्वतः पृथिवीतले।
अविभागेन भूतेषु समन्तात्सुस्थितेषु च ॥3॥
1.8.m: when the surface of the earth was completely pervaded on all sides by water, / and beings remained all around without distinction.

1.8.s:
niśāyāmiva khadyotaḥ prāvṛṭ‌kāle tatastataḥ.
tadākāśe caran so'tha vīkṣyamāṇaḥ svayambhuvaḥ ..4..
1.8.d:
निशायामिव खद्योतः प्रावृट्‌काले ततस्ततः।
तदाकाशे चरन् सोऽथ वीक्ष्यमाणः स्वयम्भुवः ॥4॥
1.8.m: Moving here and there in that space like a firefly in the night during the rainy season, / he, of Svayambhū,

1.8.s:
pratiṣṭhāyā hyapāyantu mārgamāṇastadā prabhuḥ.
tatastu salile tasmin jñātvā hyantargatāṃ mahīm ..5..
1.8.d:
प्रतिष्ठाया ह्यपायन्तु मार्गमाणस्तदा प्रभुः।
ततस्तु सलिले तस्मिन् ज्ञात्वा ह्यन्तर्गतां महीम् ॥5॥
1.8.m: seeking a support, then the Lord, / knowing the earth had entered into that water,

1.8.s:
anumānāttu sambuddho bhūmeruddharaṇaṃ prati.
cakārānyāṃ tanuñcaiva pūrvakalpādiṣu smṛtām ..6..
1.8.d:
अनुमानात्तु सम्बुद्धो भूमेरुद्धरणं प्रति।
चकारान्यां तनुञ्चैव पूर्वकल्पादिषु स्मृताम् ॥6॥
1.8.m: became aware by inference regarding the lifting of the earth, / and assumed another body remembered from the beginnings of former aeons.

1.8.s:
sa tu rūpaṃ varāhasya kṛtvā'paḥ prāviśat prabhuḥ.
adbhiḥ sañchāditāmurvīṃ samīkṣyātha prajāpatiḥ ..7..
1.8.d:
स तु रूपं वराहस्य कृत्वाऽपः प्राविशत् प्रभुः।
अद्भिः सञ्छादितामुर्वीं समीक्ष्याथ प्रजापतिः ॥7॥
1.8.m: Having assumed the form of a boar, the Lord entered the waters. / Then, beholding the earth covered with waters, Prajāpati,

1.8.s:
uddhṛtyorvīmathādbhyastu apastāstu sa vinyasat.
sāmudrīstu samudreṣu nādeyīrnimnagāsvapi.
pārthivīstu sa vinyasya pṛthivyāṃ so'cinodgirīn ..8..
1.8.d:
उद्धृत्योर्वीमथाद्भ्यस्तु अपस्तास्तु स विन्यसत्।
सामुद्रीस्तु समुद्रेषु नादेयीर्निम्नगास्वपि।
पार्थिवीस्तु स विन्यस्य पृथिव्यां सोऽचिनोद्गिरीन् ॥8॥
1.8.m: Having lifted the earth out of the waters, deposited those waters: / the oceanic [waters] into the oceans, and the riverine [waters] into the streams; / and having arranged the earthly [waters] upon the earth, he piled up the mountains.

1.8.s:
prāksarge dahyamāne tu tadā saṃvarttakāgninā.
tenāgninā pralīnāste parvatā bhuvi sarvaśaḥ ..9..
1.8.d:
प्राक्सर्गे दह्यमाने तु तदा संवर्त्तकाग्निना।
तेनाग्निना प्रलीनास्ते पर्वता भुवि सर्वशः ॥9॥
1.8.m: For when the previous creation was being consumed by the fire of cosmic dissolution, / the mountains were melted away everywhere on earth by that fire.

1.8.s:
śaityādekārṇave tasmin vāyunāpastu saṃhṛtāḥ.
niṣaktā yatra yatrāsaṃstatratatrā'calo'bhavat ..10..
1.8.d:
शैत्यादेकार्णवे तस्मिन् वायुनापस्तु संहृताः।
निषक्ता यत्र यत्रासंस्तत्रतत्राऽचलोऽभवत् ॥10॥
1.8.m: In that single vast ocean, the waters were gathered together by the wind through cold; / wherever they adhered, there an immovable [mountain] arose.

1.8.s:
skannācalatvādacalāḥ parvabhiḥ parvatāḥ smṛtāḥ.
girayo'dbhirnigīrṇatvāccayanācca śiloccayāḥ ..11..
1.8.d:
स्कन्नाचलत्वादचलाः पर्वभिः पर्वताः स्मृताः।
गिरयोऽद्भिर्निगीर्णत्वाच्चयनाच्च शिलोच्चयाः ॥11॥
1.8.m: They are called acalas because they do not move when fallen, and parvatas because of their joints (parvan). / They are called giris because they were swallowed (nigīrṇa) by the waters, and śiloccayas because they are heaps (cayana) of stones.

1.8.s:
tatastu tāṃ samuddhṛtya kṣitimantarjjalāt prabhuḥ.
svasthāne sthāpayitvā ca vibhāgamakarot punaḥ ..12..
1.8.d:
ततस्तु तां समुद्धृत्य क्षितिमन्तर्ज्जलात् प्रभुः।
स्वस्थाने स्थापयित्वा च विभागमकरोत् पुनः ॥12॥
1.8.m: Then, having lifted that earth up from within the waters / and established it in its proper place, the Lord made divisions once again.

1.8.s:
sapta sapta tu varṣāṇi tasyā dvīpeṣu saptasu.
viṣamāṇi samīkṛtya śilābhiracinodgirīn ..13..
1.8.d:
सप्त सप्त तु वर्षाणि तस्या द्वीपेषु सप्तसु।
विषमाणि समीकृत्य शिलाभिरचिनोद्गिरीन् ॥13॥
1.8.m: There were seven realms (varṣa) in each of its seven continents (dvīpa). / Having leveled the uneven regions, he piled up the mountains with rocks.

1.8.s:
dvīpeṣu teṣu varṣāṇi catvāriṃśattathaiva ca.
tāvantaḥ parvatāścaiva varṣānte samavasthitāḥ.
sargādau sanniviṣṭāste svabhāvenaiva nānyathā ..14..
1.8.d:
द्वीपेषु तेषु वर्षाणि चत्वारिंशत्तथैव च।
तावन्तः पर्वताश्चैव वर्षान्ते समवस्थिताः।
सर्गादौ सन्निविष्टास्ते स्वभावेनैव नान्यथा ॥14॥
1.8.m: And likewise, there were forty-nine realms across those continents; / and just as many mountains stood at the borders of the realms. / They were established at the beginning of creation by their very nature, not otherwise.

1.8.s:
sapta dvīpāḥ samudrāśca anyonyasya tu maṇḍalam.
sannikṛṣṭāḥ svabhāvena samāvṛtya parasparam ..15..
1.8.d:
सप्त द्वीपाः समुद्राश्च अन्योन्यस्य तु मण्डलम्।
सन्निकृष्टाः स्वभावेन समावृत्य परस्परम् ॥15॥
1.8.m: The seven continents and oceans form circles around one another, / adjoining by their very nature, mutually enclosing each other.

1.8.s:
bhūrākhyāṃścaturo lokāṃścandrādityau grahaiḥ saha.
pūrvaṃ tu nirmmame brahmā sthānānīmāni sarvaśaḥ ..16..
1.8.d:
भूराख्यांश्चतुरो लोकांश्चन्द्रादित्यौ ग्रहैः सह।
पूर्वं तु निर्म्ममे ब्रह्मा स्थानानीमानि सर्वशः ॥16॥
1.8.m: First, Brahmā fashioned the four worlds beginning with Bhūr, / along with the moon, sun, and planets, and all these places everywhere.

1.8.s:
kalpasya cāsya brahmā vai hyasṛjat sthāninaḥ purā.
āpo'griḥ pṛthivī vāyurantarikṣaṃ divaṃ tathā ..17..
1.8.d:
कल्पस्य चास्य ब्रह्मा वै ह्यसृजत् स्थानिनः पुरा।
आपोऽग्रिः पृथिवी वायुरन्तरिक्षं दिवं तथा ॥17॥
1.8.m: And at the beginning of this aeon, Brahmā created the presiding deities of the places: / waters, fire, earth, wind, the intermediate space, and heaven,

1.8.s:
svargaṃ diśaḥ samudrāṃśca nadīḥ sarvāṃśca parvatān.
oṣadhīnāṃ tathātmānamātmānaṃ vṛkṣavīrudhām ..18..
1.8.d:
स्वर्गं दिशः समुद्रांश्च नदीः सर्वांश्च पर्वतान्।
ओषधीनां तथात्मानमात्मानं वृक्षवीरुधाम् ॥18॥
1.8.m: Heaven, the quarters, the oceans, the rivers, and all the mountains; / the self of the herbs, and the self of the trees and creepers;

1.8.s:
lavāḥ kāṣṭhāḥ kalāścaiva muhūrtaṃ sandhirātryaham.
arddhamāsāṃśca māsāṃśca ayanābdayugāni ca ..19..
1.8.d:
लवाः काष्ठाः कलाश्चैव मुहूर्तं सन्धिरात्र्यहम्।
अर्द्धमासांश्च मासांश्च अयनाब्दयुगानि च ॥19॥
1.8.m: Lavas, kāṣṭhās, kalās, muhūrtas, twilight, night and day, / fortnights, months, solstices, years, and yugas.

1.8.s:
sthānābhimāninaścaiva sthānāni ca pṛthak pṛthak.
sthānātmānaḥ sa sṛṣṭvā vai yugāvasthāṃ vinirmame ..20..
1.8.d:
स्थानाभिमानिनश्चैव स्थानानि च पृथक् पृथक्।
स्थानात्मानः स सृष्ट्वा वै युगावस्थां विनिर्ममे ॥20॥
1.8.m: Having created the presiding deities of the places and the individual places, / being the soul of the places, he established the division of the yugas:

1.8.s:
kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca kaliṃ caiva tathā yugam.
kalpasyādau kṛtayuge prathame so'sṛjat prajāḥ ..21..
1.8.d:
कृतं त्रेता द्वापरं च कलिं चैव तथा युगम्।
कल्पस्यादौ कृतयुगे प्रथमे सोऽसृजत् प्रजाः ॥21॥
1.8.m: The Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, and Kali yugas. / At the beginning of the aeon, in the first Kṛtayuga, he created creatures.

1.8.s:
prāguktā yā mayā tubhyaṃ pūrvakālaṃ prajāstu tāḥ.
tasmin saṃvarttamāne tu kalpe dagdhāstadā'gninā ..22..
1.8.d:
प्रागुक्ता या मया तुभ्यं पूर्वकालं प्रजास्तु ताः।
तस्मिन् संवर्त्तमाने तु कल्पे दग्धास्तदाऽग्निना ॥22॥
1.8.m: Those creatures of earlier times, of whom I spoke to you previously, / were burned by fire when that aeon dissolved.

1.8.s:
aprāptā yāstapolokaṃ janalokaṃ samāśritāḥ.
pravartanti punaḥ sarge bījārthaṃ tā bhavanti hi ..23..
1.8.d:
अप्राप्ता यास्तपोलोकं जनलोकं समाश्रिताः।
प्रवर्तन्ति पुनः सर्गे बीजार्थं ता भवन्ति हि ॥23॥
1.8.m: Those who, not having reached Tapoloka, took refuge in Janaloka, / come forth again at the creation, for they serve as seeds.

1.8.s:
bījārthena sthitāstatra punaḥ sargasya kāraṇāt.
tatastāḥ sṛjyamānāstu santānārthaṃ bhavanti hi ..24..
1.8.d:
बीजार्थेन स्थितास्तत्र पुनः सर्गस्य कारणात्।
ततस्ताः सृज्यमानास्तु सन्तानार्थं भवन्ति हि ॥24॥
1.8.m: Stationed there as seeds for the sake of recreation, / when they are created, they exist for the sake of progeny.

1.8.s:
dharmmārthakāmamokṣāṇāmiha tāḥ sādhakāḥ smṛtāḥ.
devāśca pitaraścaiva ṛṣayo manavastathā ..25..
1.8.d:
धर्म्मार्थकाममोक्षाणामिह ताः साधकाः स्मृताः।
देवाश्च पितरश्चैव ऋषयो मनवस्तथा ॥25॥
1.8.m: They are remembered here as the achievers of dharma, purpose, pleasure, and liberation: / the gods, the ancestors, the seers, and the Manus.

1.8.s:
tataste tapasā yuktaḥ sthānānyāpūrayanti hi.
brahmaṇo mānasāste vai siddhātmāno bhavanti hi ..26..
1.8.d:
ततस्ते तपसा युक्तः स्थानान्यापूरयन्ति हि।
ब्रह्मणो मानसास्ते वै सिद्धात्मानो भवन्ति हि ॥26॥
1.8.m: Then, endowed with austerity, they fill the places; / they are indeed the mind-born sons of Brahmā, perfected in nature.

1.8.s:
ye sargā dveṣayuktena karmaṇā te divaṃ gatāḥ.
āvarttamānā iha te sambhavanti yuge yuge ..27..
1.8.d:
ये सर्गा द्वेषयुक्तेन कर्मणा ते दिवं गताः।
आवर्त्तमाना इह ते सम्भवन्ति युगे युगे ॥27॥
1.8.m: Those creations which went to heaven through action accompanied by hatred, / returning, are born here yuga after yuga.

1.8.s:
svakarmaphalaśeṣeṇa khyātāścaiva tathātmikāḥ.
saṃbhavanti janāllokāt karmasaṃśayabandhanāt ..28..
1.8.d:
स्वकर्मफलशेषेण ख्याताश्चैव तथात्मिकाः।
संभवन्ति जनाल्लोकात् कर्मसंशयबन्धनात् ॥28॥
1.8.m: Through the remainder of the fruit of their own actions, renowned and endowed with such a nature, / they are born from Janaloka through the bondage of the residue of their action.

1.8.s:
āśayaḥ kāraṇaṃ tatra boddhavyaṃ karmaṇāṃ tu saḥ.
taiḥ karmabhistu jāyante janāllokāḥ śubhāśubhaiḥ ..29..
1.8.d:
आशयः कारणं तत्र बोद्धव्यं कर्मणां तु सः।
तैः कर्मभिस्तु जायन्ते जनाल्लोकाः शुभाशुभैः ॥29॥
1.8.m: The latent trace (āśaya) is to be understood as the cause of actions there; / by those actions, auspicious and inauspicious, they are born from Janaloka.

1.8.s:
gṛhṇanti te śarīrāṇi nānārūpāṇi yoniṣu.
devādyasthāvarānte ca utpadyante parasparam ..30..
1.8.d:
गृह्णन्ति ते शरीराणि नानारूपाणि योनिषु।
देवाद्यस्थावरान्ते च उत्पद्यन्ते परस्परम् ॥30॥
1.8.m: They take on bodies of diverse forms in various wombs; / they are born among one another, from the gods down to immovable beings.

1.8.s:
teṣāṃ ye yāni karmāṇi prāk sṛṣṭeḥ pratipedire.
tānyete pratipadyante sṛjyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ ..31..
1.8.d:
तेषां ये यानि कर्माणि प्राक् सृष्टेः प्रतिपेदिरे।
तान्येते प्रतिपद्यन्ते सृज्यमानाः पुनः पुनः ॥31॥
1.8.m: Whatever actions they undertook prior to creation, / those very [actions] they undertake as they are created again and again.

1.8.s:
hisrāhiṃsre mṛdukrūre dharmādharme ṛtānṛte.
tadbhāvitāḥ prapadyante tasmāttattasya rocate ..32..
1.8.d:
हिस्राहिंस्रे मृदुक्रूरे धर्माधर्मे ऋतानृते।
तद्भाविताः प्रपद्यन्ते तस्मात्तत्तस्य रोचते ॥32॥
1.8.m: Violent or non-violent, gentle or cruel, righteous or unrighteous, true or false— / imbued with that, they assume it; therefore that pleases each of them.

1.8.s:
kalpeṣvāsan vyatīteṣu rūpanāmāni yāni ca.
tānyevānāgate kāle prāyaśaḥ pratipedire ..33..
1.8.d:
कल्पेष्वासन् व्यतीतेषु रूपनामानि यानि च।
तान्येवानागते काले प्रायशः प्रतिपेदिरे ॥33॥
1.8.m: Whatever forms and names existed in past aeons, / those very ones they mostly assumed in the time to come.

1.8.s:
tasmāttu nāmarūpāṇi tānyeva pratipedire.
punaḥ punaste kalpeṣu jāyante nāmarūpataḥ ..34..
1.8.d:
तस्मात्तु नामरूपाणि तान्येव प्रतिपेदिरे।
पुनः पुनस्ते कल्पेषु जायन्ते नामरूपतः ॥34॥
1.8.m: Therefore they assumed those very names and forms; / again and again they are born in the aeons according to name and form.

1.8.s:
tataḥ sarge hyavaṣṭabdhe sisṛkṣorbrahmaṇastu vai.
prajāstā dhyāyatastasya satyābhidhyāyinastadā ..35..
1.8.d:
ततः सर्गे ह्यवष्टब्धे सिसृक्षोर्ब्रह्मणस्तु वै।
प्रजास्ता ध्यायतस्तस्य सत्याभिध्यायिनस्तदा ॥35॥
1.8.m: Then, when creation was impeded, as Brahmā desired to create, / while he was meditating on those creatures, contemplating truth,

1.8.s:
mithunānāṃ sahasrantu so'sṛjadvai mukhāttadā.
janāste hyupapadyante sattvodriktāḥ sucetasaḥ ..36..
1.8.d:
मिथुनानां सहस्रन्तु सोऽसृजद्वै मुखात्तदा।
जनास्ते ह्युपपद्यन्ते सत्त्वोद्रिक्ताः सुचेतसः ॥36॥
1.8.m: He created a thousand pairs from his mouth; / those beings were born with sattva predominant, noble-minded.

1.8.s:
sahasramanyadvakṣasto mithunānāṃ sasarjja ha.
te sarve rajasodriktāḥ śuṣmiṇaścāpyaśuṣmiṇaḥ ..37..
1.8.d:
सहस्रमन्यद्वक्षस्तो मिथुनानां ससर्ज्ज ह।
ते सर्वे रजसोद्रिक्ताः शुष्मिणश्चाप्यशुष्मिणः ॥37॥
1.8.m: He created another thousand pairs from his chest; / they were all predominant in rajas, energetic and forceful.

1.8.s:
sṛṣṭvā sahasramanyattu dvandvānāmūrutaḥ punaḥ.
rajastamobhyāmudriktā īhāśīlāstu te smṛtāḥ ..38..
1.8.d:
सृष्ट्वा सहस्रमन्यत्तु द्वन्द्वानामूरुतः पुनः।
रजस्तमोभ्यामुद्रिक्ता ईहाशीलास्तु ते स्मृताः ॥38॥
1.8.m: Having created another thousand pairs from his thighs, / they were predominant in rajas and tamas, known to be inclined to exertion.

1.8.s:
padbhyāṃ sahasramanyattu mithunānāṃ sasarjja ha.
udriktāstamasā sarve niḥśrīkā hyalpatejasaḥ ..39..
1.8.d:
पद्भ्यां सहस्रमन्यत्तु मिथुनानां ससर्ज्ज ह।
उद्रिक्तास्तमसा सर्वे निःश्रीका ह्यल्पतेजसः ॥39॥
1.8.m: He created another thousand pairs from his feet; / all were predominant in tamas, destitute of splendor and of little vigor.

1.8.s:
tato vai harṣamānāste dvandvotpannāstu prāṇinaḥ.
anyonyā hṛcchapāvipṭā maithunāyopacakramuḥ ..40..
1.8.d:
ततो वै हर्षमानास्ते द्वन्द्वोत्पन्नास्तु प्राणिनः।
अन्योन्या हृच्छपाविप्टा मैथुनायोपचक्रमुः ॥40॥
1.8.m: Then, rejoicing, those living beings born in pairs, / seized with desire for one another, engaged in copulation.

1.8.s:
tataḥprabhṛti kalpe'smin mithunotpattirucyate.
māse māserttavaṃ yadyattadājñāsiddhi yoṣitāt ..41..
1.8.d:
ततःप्रभृति कल्पेऽस्मिन् मिथुनोत्पत्तिरुच्यते।
मासे मासेर्त्तवं यद्यत्तदाज्ञासिद्धि योषितात् ॥41॥
1.8.m: From that time forth, the birth of pairs is proclaimed in this aeon. / Month by month was their season, for women then conceived merely by thought.

1.8.s:
tasmāttadā na suṣuvuḥ sevitairapi maithunaiḥ.
āyuṣo'nte prasūyante mithunānyeva te sakṛt ..42..
1.8.d:
तस्मात्तदा न सुषुवुः सेवितैरपि मैथुनैः।
आयुषोऽन्ते प्रसूयन्ते मिथुनान्येव ते सकृत् ॥42॥
1.8.m: Therefore they did not give birth then, even when engaging in intercourse; / only at the end of their lifespan did they give birth to pairs, just once.

1.8.s:
kuṭakāḥ kuvikāścaiva utpadyante mumūrṣitāḥ.
tataḥprabhṛti kalpe'smin mithunānāṃ hi sambhavaḥ ..43..
1.8.d:
कुटकाः कुविकाश्चैव उत्पद्यन्ते मुमूर्षिताः।
ततःप्रभृति कल्पेऽस्मिन् मिथुनानां हि सम्भवः ॥43॥
1.8.m: Pairs of sons and daughters were born to them as they were about to die; / from that time forth, indeed, pairs have come into being in this aeon.

1.8.s:
dhyāte tu manasā tāsāṃ prajānāṃ jāyate sakṛt.
śabdādi viṣayaḥ śuddhaḥ pratyekaṃ pañcalakṣaṇaḥ ..44..
1.8.d:
ध्याते तु मनसा तासां प्रजानां जायते सकृत्।
शब्दादि विषयः शुद्धः प्रत्येकं पञ्चलक्षणः ॥44॥
1.8.m: When meditated upon with the mind, the pure fivefold object [of the senses]— / sound and the rest—arose for those creatures at once, each distinct.

1.8.s:
ityevaṃ manasā pūrvaṃ prāksṛṣṭiryā prajāpateḥ.
tasyānvavāye sambhūtā yairidaṃ pūritaṃ jagat ..45..
1.8.d:
इत्येवं मनसा पूर्वं प्राक्सृष्टिर्या प्रजापतेः।
तस्यान्ववाये सम्भूता यैरिदं पूरितं जगत् ॥45॥
1.8.m: In this way, the early creation of Prajāpati was previously made by mind; / in his lineage they were born, by whom this world was filled.

1.8.s:
saritsaraḥ samudrāṃśca sevante parvatānapi.
tadā nātyambuśītoṣṇā yuge tasmin caranti vai ..46..
1.8.d:
सरित्सरः समुद्रांश्च सेवन्ते पर्वतानपि।
तदा नात्यम्बुशीतोष्णा युगे तस्मिन् चरन्ति वै ॥46॥
1.8.m: They resorted to rivers, lakes, oceans, and mountains; / in that yuga they wandered about, neither overly wet, cold, nor hot.

1.8.s:
pṛthvīrasodbhavaṃ nāma āhāraṃ hyāharanti vai.
tāḥ prajāḥ kāmacāriṇyo mānasīṃ siddhimāsthitāḥ ..47..
1.8.d:
पृथ्वीरसोद्भवं नाम आहारं ह्याहरन्ति वै।
ताः प्रजाः कामचारिण्यो मानसीं सिद्धिमास्थिताः ॥47॥
1.8.m: They consumed the food called the essence of the earth; / moving at will, those creatures possessed mental perfection.

1.8.s:
dharmādharmau na tāsvāstāṃ nirviśeṣāḥ prajāstu tāḥ.
tulyamāyuḥ sukhaṃ rūpaṃ tāsāṃ tasmin kṛte yuge ..48..
1.8.d:
धर्माधर्मौ न तास्वास्तां निर्विशेषाः प्रजास्तु ताः।
तुल्यमायुः सुखं रूपं तासां तस्मिन् कृते युगे ॥48॥
1.8.m: Neither righteousness nor unrighteousness existed among them; those creatures were without distinctions; / their lifespan, happiness, and beauty were equal in that Kṛtayuga.

1.8.s:
dharmādharmau na tāsvāstāṃ kalpādau tu kṛte yuge.
svena svenādhikāreṇa jajñire te kṛte yuge ..49..
1.8.d:
धर्माधर्मौ न तास्वास्तां कल्पादौ तु कृते युगे।
स्वेन स्वेनाधिकारेण जज्ञिरे ते कृते युगे ॥49॥
1.8.m: Neither righteousness nor unrighteousness existed among them at the beginning of the aeon in the Kṛtayuga; / they were born in the Kṛtayuga, each with their own capacity.

1.8.s:
catvāri tu sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ divyasaṃkhyayā.
ādyaṃ kṛtayugaṃ prāhuḥ sandhyānāntu catuḥ śatam ..50..
1.8.d:
चत्वारि तु सहस्राणि वर्षाणां दिव्यसंख्यया।
आद्यं कृतयुगं प्राहुः सन्ध्यानान्तु चतुः शतम् ॥50॥
1.8.m: They say the first Kṛtayuga lasts four thousand years / by divine reckoning, and its dawn consists of four hundred [years].

1.8.s:
tataḥ sahasraśastāsu prajāsu prathitāsvapi.
na tāsāṃ pratighāto'sti na dvandvannāpi ca kramaḥ ..51..
1.8.d:
ततः सहस्रशस्तासु प्रजासु प्रथितास्वपि।
न तासां प्रतिघातोऽस्ति न द्वन्द्वन्नापि च क्रमः ॥51॥
1.8.m: Then, even as those creatures multiplied by the thousands, / there was no obstacle for them, no pair of opposites, and no gradation of rank.

1.8.s:
parvatodadhisevinyo hyaniketāśrayāstu tāḥ.
viśokāḥ sattvabahulā ekāntasukhitaprajāḥ ..52..
1.8.d:
पर्वतोदधिसेविन्यो ह्यनिकेताश्रयास्तु ताः।
विशोकाः सत्त्वबहुला एकान्तसुखितप्रजाः ॥52॥
1.8.m: Resorting to mountains and oceans, they lived without dwellings; / free from sorrow, abundant in sattva, those creatures were exceedingly happy.

1.8.s:
tā vai nikāmacāriṇyo nityaṃ muditamānasāḥ.
paśavaḥ pakṣiṇaścaiva na tadāsan sarīsṛpāḥ ..53..
1.8.d:
ता वै निकामचारिण्यो नित्यं मुदितमानसाः।
पशवः पक्षिणश्चैव न तदासन् सरीसृपाः ॥53॥
1.8.m: Moving about entirely at will, their minds were ever joyful. / At that time there were no beasts, no birds, and no reptiles,

1.8.s:
nodbhijjā nārakāścaiva te hyadharmaprasūtayaḥ.
na mūlaphalapuṣpañca nārttavaṃ hyṛtavo na ca ..54..
1.8.d:
नोद्भिज्जा नारकाश्चैव ते ह्यधर्मप्रसूतयः।
न मूलफलपुष्पञ्च नार्त्तवं ह्यृतवो न च ॥54॥
1.8.m: nor plants born from sprouting, nor hell-beings, for such are born of adharma. / There were no roots, fruits, or flowers, no seasonal produce, and no seasons.

1.8.s:
sarvakāmasukhaḥ kālo nātyarthaṃ hyuṣṇaśītatā.
manobhilaṣitāḥ kāmāstāsāṃ sarvatra sarvadā ..55..
1.8.d:
सर्वकामसुखः कालो नात्यर्थं ह्युष्णशीतता।
मनोभिलषिताः कामास्तासां सर्वत्र सर्वदा ॥55॥
1.8.m: The time was delightful for all desires, without excessive heat or cold. / The objects desired in their minds were always present everywhere for them.

1.8.s:
uttiṣṭhanti pṛthivyāṃ vai tābhirdhyātā rasotthitāḥ.
balavarṇakarī tāsāṃ siddhiḥ sā roganāśinī ..56..
1.8.d:
उत्तिष्ठन्ति पृथिव्यां वै ताभिर्ध्याता रसोत्थिताः।
बलवर्णकरी तासां सिद्धिः सा रोगनाशिनी ॥56॥
1.8.m: Whenever meditated upon by them, things arising from the essence [of earth] sprang up on the earth. / That perfection brought them strength and complexion, and destroyed all disease.

1.8.s:
asaṃskāryaiḥ śarīraiśca prajāstāḥ sthirayauvanāḥ.
tāsāṃ viśuddhāt saṅkalpājjāyante mithunāḥ prajāḥ ..57..
1.8.d:
असंस्कार्यैः शरीरैश्च प्रजास्ताः स्थिरयौवनाः।
तासां विशुद्धात् सङ्कल्पाज्जायन्ते मिथुनाः प्रजाः ॥57॥
1.8.m: With bodies needing no adornment or purificatory rites, those creatures had unchanging youth. / Through their pure intention alone, offspring were born in pairs [of male and female].

1.8.s:
samaṃ janma ca rūpañca mriyante caiva tāḥ samam.
tadā satyamalobhaśca kṣamā tuṣṭiḥ sukhaṃ damaḥ ..58..
1.8.d:
समं जन्म च रूपञ्च म्रियन्ते चैव ताः समम्।
तदा सत्यमलोभश्च क्षमा तुष्टिः सुखं दमः ॥58॥
1.8.m: Their birth and appearance were identical, and they died at the very same time. / In those days there were truthfulness, freedom from greed, forbearance, contentment, happiness, and self-restraint.

1.8.s:
nirviśeṣāḥ kṛtāḥ sarvā rūpāyuḥśīlaceṣṭitaiḥ.
abuddhipūrvakaṃ vṛttaṃ prajānāṃ jāyate svayam ..59..
1.8.d:
निर्विशेषाः कृताः सर्वा रूपायुःशीलचेष्टितैः।
अबुद्धिपूर्वकं वृत्तं प्रजानां जायते स्वयम् ॥59॥
1.8.m: All were created without distinction in beauty, lifespan, character, and conduct. / The conduct of those creatures arose spontaneously, without premeditation.

1.8.s:
apravṛttiḥ kṛtayuge karmaṇoḥ śubhapāpayoḥ.
varṇāśramavyavasthāśca na tadāsanna saṅkaraḥ ..60..
1.8.d:
अप्रवृत्तिः कृतयुगे कर्मणोः शुभपापयोः।
वर्णाश्रमव्यवस्थाश्च न तदासन्न सङ्करः ॥60॥
1.8.m: In the Kṛta Yuga there was no undertaking of good or bad actions. / There were then no distinctions of classes and life stages, nor any mingling of classes.

1.8.s:
anicchādveṣayuktāste varttayanti parasparam.
tulyarūpāyuṣaḥ sarvā adhamottamavarjjitāḥ ..61..
1.8.d:
अनिच्छाद्वेषयुक्तास्ते वर्त्तयन्ति परस्परम्।
तुल्यरूपायुषः सर्वा अधमोत्तमवर्ज्जिताः ॥61॥
1.8.m: Devoid of desire and hatred, they lived with one another. / All were equal in form and lifespan, free from low and high.

1.8.s:
sukhaprāyā hyaśokāśca utpadyante kṛte yuge.
nityaprahṛṣṭamanaso mahāsattvā mahābalāḥ ..62..
1.8.d:
सुखप्राया ह्यशोकाश्च उत्पद्यन्ते कृते युगे।
नित्यप्रहृष्टमनसो महासत्त्वा महाबलाः ॥62॥
1.8.m: Born in the Kṛta Yuga, they were largely happy and free from sorrow, / with ever-delighted minds, of great sattva, and possessing immense strength.

1.8.s:
lābhālābhau nāsvāstāṃ mitrāmitre priyāpriye.
manasā viṣayastāsānnirīhāṇāṃ pravarttate.
na lipsanti hi tā'nyonyannānugṛhṇanti caiva hi ..63..
1.8.d:
लाभालाभौ नास्वास्तां मित्रामित्रे प्रियाप्रिये।
मनसा विषयस्तासान्निरीहाणां प्रवर्त्तते।
न लिप्सन्ति हि ताऽन्योन्यन्नानुगृह्णन्ति चैव हि ॥63॥
1.8.m: They knew neither gain nor loss, neither friend nor enemy, neither pleasant nor unpleasant. / By thought alone an object arose for them, who were free from longing; / they did not covet one another's [belongings], nor did they show favor to one another.

1.8.s:
dhyānaṃ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ jñānamucyate.
pravṛttaṃ dvāpare yajñaṃ dānaṃ kaliyuge varam ..64..
1.8.d:
ध्यानं परं कृतयुगे त्रेतायां ज्ञानमुच्यते।
प्रवृत्तं द्वापरे यज्ञं दानं कलियुगे वरम् ॥64॥
1.8.m: Meditation is supreme in the Kṛta Yuga; knowledge is said to be [supreme] in Tretā. / Sacrifice is instituted in Dvāpara; generosity is the best [practice] in the Kali Yuga.

1.8.s:
sattvaṃ kṛtaṃ rajastretā dvāparantu rajastamau.
kalau tamastu vijñeyaṃ yugavṛttavaśena tu ..65..
1.8.d:
सत्त्वं कृतं रजस्त्रेता द्वापरन्तु रजस्तमौ।
कलौ तमस्तु विज्ञेयं युगवृत्तवशेन तु ॥65॥
1.8.m: Kṛta is sattva, Tretā is rajas, Dvāpara is rajas and tamas, / and Kali is to be known as tamas, due to the influence of the conduct of the yugas.

1.8.s:
kālaḥ kṛte yuge tveṣa tasya saṃkhyānnibodhata.
catvāri tu sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ tta kṛtaṃ yugam ..66..
1.8.d:
कालः कृते युगे त्वेष तस्य संख्यान्निबोधत।
चत्वारि तु सहस्राणि वर्षाणां त्त कृतं युगम् ॥66॥
1.8.m: This is the time of the Kṛta Yuga; now learn its calculation: / the Kṛta Yuga consists of four thousand divine years.

1.8.s:
sandhyāṃśau tasya divyāni śatānyaṣṭau ca saṃkhyayā.
tadā tāsāṃ babhūvāyurnna ca kleśavipattayaḥ ..67..
1.8.d:
सन्ध्यांशौ तस्य दिव्यानि शतान्यष्टौ च संख्यया।
तदा तासां बभूवायुर्न्न च क्लेशविपत्तयः ॥67॥
1.8.m: Its two twilight periods number eight hundred divine [years]. / Such was their lifespan at that time, and there were no afflictions or calamities.

1.8.s:
tataḥ kṛtayuge tasmin sandhyāṃśe hi gate tu vaiḥ.
pādāvaśiṣṭo bhavati yugadharmastu sarvaśaḥ ..68..
1.8.d:
ततः कृतयुगे तस्मिन् सन्ध्यांशे हि गते तु वैः।
पादावशिष्टो भवति युगधर्मस्तु सर्वशः ॥68॥
1.8.m: Then, when the twilight period of that Kṛta Yuga had passed, / the virtue of the yuga, in all respects, came to remain in only one fourth.

1.8.s:
sandhyāyāmapyatītāyāmantakāle yugasya tu.
pādataśvāvatiṣṭhettu sandhyādharmo yugasya tu.
evaṃ kṛte tu niḥśeṣe siddhi stvantardadhe tadā ..69..
1.8.d:
सन्ध्यायामप्यतीतायामन्तकाले युगस्य तु।
पादतश्वावतिष्ठेत्तु सन्ध्याधर्मो युगस्य तु।
एवं कृते तु निःशेषे सिद्धि स्त्वन्तर्दधे तदा ॥69॥
1.8.m: Even when the dawn had elapsed at the conclusion of the yuga, / the virtue of the yuga's dawn stood in one fourth. / Thus, when the Kṛta [Yuga] was completely exhausted, that perfection vanished.

1.8.s:
tasyāñca siddhau bhraṣṭāyāṃ mānasyāmabhavattataḥ.
siddhiranyā yuge tasmistretāyāmantare kṛtāḥ ..70..
1.8.d:
तस्याञ्च सिद्धौ भ्रष्टायां मानस्यामभवत्ततः।
सिद्धिरन्या युगे तस्मिस्त्रेतायामन्तरे कृताः ॥70॥
1.8.m: When that mental perfection had been lost, then / another perfection arose in that yuga, created within the Tretā [Yuga].

1.8.s:
sargādau yā mayāṣṭau tu mānasyo vai prakīrttitāḥ.
aṣṭau tāḥ kramayogena siddhayo yānti saṃkṣayam ..71..
1.8.d:
सर्गादौ या मयाष्टौ तु मानस्यो वै प्रकीर्त्तिताः।
अष्टौ ताः क्रमयोगेन सिद्धयो यान्ति संक्षयम् ॥71॥
1.8.m: The eight mental perfections that were proclaimed by me at the beginning of creation— / those eight perfections gradually go to destruction.

1.8.s:
kalpādau mānasī hyeṣā siddhirbhavati sā kṛte.
manvantareṣu sarveṣu caturyugavibhāgaśaḥ.
varṇāśramācārakṛtaḥ karmasiddhodbhavaḥ smṛtaḥ ..72..
1.8.d:
कल्पादौ मानसी ह्येषा सिद्धिर्भवति सा कृते।
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु चतुर्युगविभागशः।
वर्णाश्रमाचारकृतः कर्मसिद्धोद्भवः स्मृतः ॥72॥
1.8.m: This mental perfection occurs in the Kṛta [Yuga] at the start of an aeon. / In all cosmic ages of a Manu, according to the division of the four yugas, / the arising of perfection through action is remembered to be produced by the conduct of the classes and stages of life.

1.8.s:
sandhyākṛtasya pādena sandhyāpādena cāṃśataḥ.
kṛtasandhyāṃśakā hyete trīṃstrīn pādān parasparān.
hrasanti yugadharmaiste tapaḥ śrutabalāyuṣaiḥ ..73..
1.8.d:
सन्ध्याकृतस्य पादेन सन्ध्यापादेन चांशतः।
कृतसन्ध्यांशका ह्येते त्रींस्त्रीन् पादान् परस्परान्।
ह्रसन्ति युगधर्मैस्ते तपः श्रुतबलायुषैः ॥73॥
1.8.m: By a fourth of the dawn-portion of the Kṛta, and by a fourth of the twilight-portion, / these dawn and twilight portions of the Kṛta [and other yugas], / in each case diminishing by three quarters, decrease in the virtues of the yugas—in asceticism, sacred learning, strength, and lifespan.

1.8.s:
tataḥ kṛtāṃśe kṣīṇe tu babhūva tadanantaram.
tretāyāṃ yugamanyantu kṛtāśamṛṣisattamāḥ ..74..
1.8.d:
ततः कृतांशे क्षीणे तु बभूव तदनन्तरम्।
त्रेतायां युगमन्यन्तु कृताशमृषिसत्तमाः ॥74॥
1.8.m: Then, when the portion of the Kṛta was exhausted, immediately thereafter, / another yuga began in the Tretā, consisting of [traces of] the Kṛta, O best of seers.

1.8.s:
tasmin kṣīṇe kṛtāṃśe tu tacchiṣṭāsu prajāsviha.
kalpādau saṃpravṛttāyāstretāyāḥ pramukhe tadā ..75..
1.8.d:
तस्मिन् क्षीणे कृतांशे तु तच्छिष्टासु प्रजास्विह।
कल्पादौ संप्रवृत्तायास्त्रेतायाः प्रमुखे तदा ॥75॥
1.8.m: When that portion of the Kṛta had waned among the creatures remaining here, / at the very beginning of the Tretā which had commenced at the start of the aeon,

1.8.s:
praṇaśyati tadā siddhiḥ kālayogena nānyathā.
tasyāṃ siddhau praṇaṣṭāyāmanyā siddhiravarttata ..76..
1.8.d:
प्रणश्यति तदा सिद्धिः कालयोगेन नान्यथा।
तस्यां सिद्धौ प्रणष्टायामन्या सिद्धिरवर्त्तत ॥76॥
1.8.m: perfection then perishes through the influence of time and not otherwise. / When that perfection had perished, another perfection operated.

1.8.s:
apāṃ saukṣmye pratigate tadā meghātmanā tu tau.
meghebhyastanayitnubhyaḥ pravṛttaṃ vṛṣṭisarjjanam ..77..
1.8.d:
अपां सौक्ष्म्ये प्रतिगते तदा मेघात्मना तु तौ।
मेघेभ्यस्तनयित्नुभ्यः प्रवृत्तं वृष्टिसर्ज्जनम् ॥77॥
1.8.m: When the subtleness of the waters had passed away, then both [subtleness and moisture took] the form of clouds; / and from the thundering clouds the pouring forth of rain began.

1.8.s:
sakṛdeva tayā vṛṣṭyā saṃyukte pṛthivītale.
prādurāsaṃstadā tāsāṃ vṛkṣāstu gṛhasaṃsthitāḥ ..78..
1.8.d:
सकृदेव तया वृष्ट्या संयुक्ते पृथिवीतले।
प्रादुरासंस्तदा तासां वृक्षास्तु गृहसंस्थिताः ॥78॥
1.8.m: No sooner had the surface of the earth been touched by that rain / than trees serving as dwellings appeared for them.

1.8.s:
sarvapratyupabhogastu tāsāṃ tebhyaḥ prajāyate.
varttayanti hi tebhyastāstretāyugamukhe prajāḥ ..79..
1.8.d:
सर्वप्रत्युपभोगस्तु तासां तेभ्यः प्रजायते।
वर्त्तयन्ति हि तेभ्यस्तास्त्रेतायुगमुखे प्रजाः ॥79॥
1.8.m: Every kind of enjoyment was produced for them from those [trees]; / indeed, those creatures maintained themselves from them at the beginning of the Tretā Yuga.

1.8.s:
tataḥ kālena mahatā tāsāmeva viparyayāt.
rāgalobhātmako bhāvastadā hyākasmiko'bhavat ..80..
1.8.d:
ततः कालेन महता तासामेव विपर्ययात्।
रागलोभात्मको भावस्तदा ह्याकस्मिकोऽभवत् ॥80॥
1.8.m: Then, after a great length of time, due to their very degeneration, / a state of mind characterized by passion and greed suddenly arose [in them].

1.8.s:
yattadbhavati nārīṇāṃ jīvitānte tadārttavam.
tadā tadvai na bhavati punaryugabalena tu ..81..
1.8.d:
यत्तद्भवति नारीणां जीवितान्ते तदार्त्तवम्।
तदा तद्वै न भवति पुनर्युगबलेन तु ॥81॥
1.8.m: That menstruation which occurs in women [only] at the end of their lives— / that ceased to be so, once again through the force of the yuga.

1.8.s:
tāsāṃ punaḥ pravṛttaṃ tu māse māse tadārttavam.
tatastenaiva yogena varttatāṃ mithune tadā ..82..
tāsāṃ tatkālabhāvitvānmāsi māsyupagacchatām.
akāle hyārttavotpattirgarbhotpattirajāyata ..83..
1.8.d:
तासां पुनः प्रवृत्तं तु मासे मासे तदार्त्तवम्।
ततस्तेनैव योगेन वर्त्ततां मिथुने तदा ॥82॥
तासां तत्कालभावित्वान्मासि मास्युपगच्छताम्।
अकाले ह्यार्त्तवोत्पत्तिर्गर्भोत्पत्तिरजायत ॥83॥
1.8.m: Their menstruation began to occur again month after month. / Then, by that very development, as they lived in couples at that time, / because they came together month after month owing to the condition of the time, / the occurrence of menstruation and the formation of embryos happened untimely.

1.8.s:
viparyayeṇa tāsāṃ tu tena kālena bhāvinā.
praṇaśyanti tataḥ sarve vṛkṣāste gṛhasaṃsthitāḥ ..84..
1.8.d:
विपर्ययेण तासां तु तेन कालेन भाविना।
प्रणश्यन्ति ततः सर्वे वृक्षास्ते गृहसंस्थिताः ॥84॥
1.8.m: Due to their degeneration, brought about by that time, / all those trees that served as dwellings then perished.

1.8.s:
tatasteṣu praṇaṣṭeṣu vibhrāntā vyākulendriyāḥ.
abhi dhyāyanti tāṃ siddhiṃ satyābhidhyāyinastadā ..85..
1.8.d:
ततस्तेषु प्रणष्टेषु विभ्रान्ता व्याकुलेन्द्रियाः।
अभि ध्यायन्ति तां सिद्धिं सत्याभिध्यायिनस्तदा ॥85॥
1.8.m: Then, when those [trees] had perished, bewildered and with agitated senses, / meditating on truth, they then meditated on that perfection.

1.8.s:
prādurbabhūvustāsāṃ ca vṛkṣāste gṛhasaṃsthitāḥ.
vastrāṇi ca prasūyante phalānyābharaṇāni ca ..86..
1.8.d:
प्रादुर्बभूवुस्तासां च वृक्षास्ते गृहसंस्थिताः।
वस्त्राणि च प्रसूयन्ते फलान्याभरणानि च ॥86॥
1.8.m: And for them there appeared trees that served as dwellings; / and they produced garments, fruits, and ornaments.

1.8.s:
teṣveva jāyate tāsāṃ gaṃdhavarṇarasānvitam.
amākṣikaṃ mahāvīryaṃ puṭake puṭake madhu ..87..
1.8.d:
तेष्वेव जायते तासां गंधवर्णरसान्वितम्।
अमाक्षिकं महावीर्यं पुटके पुटके मधु ॥87॥
1.8.m: In those very [trees] there was born for them, in hollow after hollow, / a honey made without bees, endowed with fragrance, color, and taste, of great potency.

1.8.s:
tena tā vartayanti sma mukhe tretāyugasya ca.
hṛṣṭatuṣṭāstayā siddhyā prajā vai vigatajvarāḥ ..88..
1.8.d:
तेन ता वर्तयन्ति स्म मुखे त्रेतायुगस्य च।
हृष्टतुष्टास्तया सिद्ध्या प्रजा वै विगतज्वराः ॥88॥
1.8.m: They sustained themselves by that at the opening of the Tretā Yuga; / delighted and contented with that perfection, the creatures were free from suffering.

1.8.s:
punaḥ kālāṃtareṇaiva punarllobhāvṛtāstu tāḥ.
vṛkṣāṃstān paryagṛhṇanta madhu vā mākṣikaṃ balāt ..89..
1.8.d:
पुनः कालांतरेणैव पुनर्ल्लोभावृतास्तु ताः।
वृक्षांस्तान् पर्यगृह्णन्त मधु वा माक्षिकं बलात् ॥89॥
1.8.m: Then, after another interval of time, overcome once more by greed, / they seized those trees or took the honey forcibly.

1.8.s:
tāsāṃ tenāpacāreṇa punarllokakṛtena vai.
praṇaṣṭā madhunā sārddhaṃ kalpavṛkṣāḥ vkacit vkacit ..90..
1.8.d:
तासां तेनापचारेण पुनर्ल्लोककृतेन वै।
प्रणष्टा मधुना सार्द्धं कल्पवृक्षाः व्कचित् व्कचित् ॥90॥
1.8.m: Due to that offense committed once again by the people, / the wish-fulfilling trees, along with the honey, perished here and there.

1.8.s:
tasyāmevālpaśiṣṭāyāṃ saṃdhyākālavaśāttadā.
prāvartaṃta tadā tāsāṃ dvaṃdvānyabhyutthitāni tu ..91..
1.8.d:
तस्यामेवाल्पशिष्टायां संध्याकालवशात्तदा।
प्रावर्तंत तदा तासां द्वंद्वान्यभ्युत्थितानि तु ॥91॥
1.8.m: When only a little of it remained, then, under the influence of the twilight period, / pairs of opposites arose and began to affect them.

1.8.s: śītavātātapaistīvraistatastā duḥkhitā bhṛśam..
1.8.d: शीतवातातपैस्तीव्रैस्ततस्ता दुःखिता भृशम्॥
1.8.m:
Then they were severely distressed by severe cold, wind, and heat;
afflicted by the pairs of opposites, they built shelters.

1.8.s: dvaṃdvaistāḥ pīḍyamānāstu cakrurāvaraṇāni ca ..92..
1.8.d: द्वंद्वैस्ताः पीड्यमानास्तु चक्रुरावरणानि च ॥92॥

1.8.s:
kṛtvā dvaṃdva pratīkāraṃ niketāni hi bhojire.
pūrvaṃ nikamipārāste aniketāśrayā bhṛśam ..93..
1.8.d:
कृत्वा द्वंद्व प्रतीकारं निकेतानि हि भोजिरे।
पूर्वं निकमिपारास्ते अनिकेताश्रया भृशम् ॥93॥
1.8.m: Having countered the pairs of opposites, they enjoyed homes; / previously, acting entirely at will, they had lived without dwellings.

1.8.s:
yathāyogyaṃ yathāprīti niketeṣvavasan punaḥ.
marudhanvasu nimneṣu parvateṣu nadīṣu ca.
saṃśrayanti ca durgāṇi dhanvānaṃ śāśvatodakam ..94..
1.8.d:
यथायोग्यं यथाप्रीति निकेतेष्ववसन् पुनः।
मरुधन्वसु निम्नेषु पर्वतेषु नदीषु च।
संश्रयन्ति च दुर्गाणि धन्वानं शाश्वतोदकम् ॥94॥
1.8.m: They lived again in dwellings according to suitability and according to desire, / in desert wildernesses, lowlands, mountains, and rivers; / and they took refuge in fortresses, in the desert, and in places with perpetual water.

1.8.s:
yathāyogaṃ yathākāmaṃ sameṣu viṣameṣu ca.
ārabdhāste niketā vai karttaṃ śītoṣṇa vāraṇam ..95..
1.8.d:
यथायोगं यथाकामं समेषु विषमेषु च।
आरब्धास्ते निकेता वै कर्त्तं शीतोष्ण वारणम् ॥95॥
1.8.m: According to fitness and according to wish, on level ground and on uneven ground, / they began to build dwellings to ward off cold and heat.

1.8.s:
tataḥ saṃsthāpayāmāsa kheṭāni ca purāṇi ca.
grāmāṃścaiva yathābhāgaṃ tathaivāntaḥ purāṇi ca ..96..
1.8.d:
ततः संस्थापयामास खेटानि च पुराणि च।
ग्रामांश्चैव यथाभागं तथैवान्तः पुराणि च ॥96॥
1.8.m: Then they founded hamlets and cities, / and villages according to division, and likewise royal palaces.

1.8.s:
tāsāmāyāmaviṣkambhān saṃniveśāntarāṇi ca.
cakrustadā yathāprajñaṃ pradeśaḥ saṃjñitastu taiḥ ..97..
1.8.d:
तासामायामविष्कम्भान् संनिवेशान्तराणि च।
चक्रुस्तदा यथाप्रज्ञं प्रदेशः संज्ञितस्तु तैः ॥97॥
1.8.m: They laid out their lengths, breadths, and intermediate spaces / at that time according to their intelligence, with measurements designated by them.

1.8.s:
aṃguṣṭhasya pradeśinyā vyāsaḥ prādeśa ucyate.
tālaḥ smṛto madhyamayā gokarṇaścāpyanāmayā ..98..
1.8.d:
अंगुष्ठस्य प्रदेशिन्या व्यासः प्रादेश उच्यते।
तालः स्मृतो मध्यमया गोकर्णश्चाप्यनामया ॥98॥
1.8.m: The span between the thumb and forefinger is called a prādeśa; / that with the middle finger is known as a tāla, and with the ring finger a gokarṇa;

1.8.s:
kaniṣṭhayā vitastistu dvādaśāṅula ucyate.
ratniraṅgulaparvvāṇi saṃkhyayā tvekaviṃśatiḥ ..99..
1.8.d:
कनिष्ठया वितस्तिस्तु द्वादशाङुल उच्यते।
रत्निरङ्गुलपर्व्वाणि संख्यया त्वेकविंशतिः ॥99॥
1.8.m: with the little finger it is a vitasti, said to be twelve aṅgulas. / An aratni is counted as twenty-one joints of fingers;

1.8.s:
caturviṃśatibhiścaiva hastaḥ syādaṅgulāni tu.
